---
lang: en
format:
  typst:
    pdf-standard: ua-1
    papersize: a4
    fontsize: 9pt
    margin:
      top: 2.1cm
      bottom: 1.9cm
      left: 1.7cm
      right: 1.7cm
    mainfont: "Segoe UI"
    section-numbering: ""
brand:
  color:
    palette:
      paper: "#FFFFFF"
      ink: "#22282E"
      ink-soft: "#5C666F"
      red: "#C10016"
      blue: "#0F4C81"
    background: paper
    foreground: ink
    primary: blue

  # No font is named beyond the one above, so nothing is fetched from a font
  # service; a system without it falls back to the default of the renderer.
  typography:
    headings:
      weight: bold
      color: red
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    echo: false
    message: false
    warning: false
    dev: "ragg_png"
    dev.args: {bg: "white"}
    dpi: 300
    fig-width: 6.8
    fig-height: 2.5
execute:
  # A chunk that fails stops the render. This is Quarto's default and is
  # named here because the opposite was set once: under `error: true` a
  # report whose chunks had all failed still rendered and still exited 0 --
  # the coverage report over a lake it could not read produced a PDF whose
  # pages were `object 'period_end' not found` -- and a scheduler only sees
  # the exit code. Inline `r` does not honour the setting either way, so
  # under `error: true` the render died at the first inline reference to a
  # variable the failed chunk never created, three sections past the fault.
  error: false
---

```{r setup}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What to set for a filer
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The path to the config file, whose edinet section names the Silver layer of
# the module. A chunk runs with the directory of this template as its working
# directory, which is inside the installed package, so the path is taken from
# the environment variable FINCOMMONS_CONFIG where it is set and is otherwise
# a paths.yaml beside the template.
config_path <- Sys.getenv("FINCOMMONS_CONFIG", "paths.yaml")

# The filer, by its EDINET code: the letter E and five digits, which is how
# the agency addresses a filer and how the Silver layer spells it. This is
# Kojima Co., Ltd., a listed electronics retailer closing in August; any
# other filer whose annual report the edinet pipeline has collected can be
# put here. The securities code is not it: Kojima is 7513 on the exchange and
# E03270 in EDINET.
filer_edinet_code <- "E03270"

# The number of financial years shown. The Japanese annual securities report
# carries a five-year summary of the headline figures in its own front
# matter, so five is what one report affords and more needs more reports.
n_years <- 5

# Which report a figure is taken from, where several state the same year.
#
#   "as-reported"  the year's own annual report. A figure in the column of a
#                  year is the one the market saw when that year was
#                  reported, and the four earlier years of a five-year
#                  summary are left to the reports whose own years they are
#                  wherever the lake holds them.
#   "latest"       the most recently filed report that states the year, which
#                  is the restated figure wherever the filer restated it.
#
# With one report in the lake the two are the same, that report being both.
# Every figure that is not the year's own is marked with a dagger (†).
basis <- "as-reported"

# Which set of statements to read.
#
#   "auto"              the consolidated accounts where the filing says it
#                       prepared them, and the parent's own where it says it
#                       did not
#   "consolidated"      the group, and a dash for a filer that has none
#   "nonconsolidated"   the parent alone, for every filer
#
# This is the first decision a Japanese report asks for and it is not a
# formality: a filing that consolidates states every figure of its summary
# and of its statements twice, once for the group and once for the parent
# alone, and the two are far apart. Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu reports earnings per
# share of 294.99 for the group and 236.58 for the parent in the same table
# of the same report. See the chunk on the consolidation basis below for how
# the two are told apart.
consolidation <- "auto"

# The language of the labels in the tables.
#
#   "en"    the English names this template carries
#   "ja"    the Japanese labels the conversion states beside each element
#   "both"  the English name and the filer's own label under it
#
# The agency's conversion gives no English label, so "en" is this template's
# own naming of the elements and "ja" is the filing's. Charts use the English
# names whatever this is set to, their font being the one the corporate
# design names rather than the one the page is set in.
labels <- "en"

# The font the Japanese text is set in. The page is set in the font the
# design names, which covers no Japanese, so a second font is named for the
# characters the first one lacks: a filer's name, an industry, an address and
# every label under "ja" or "both" are Japanese, and without a fallback typst
# sets them as empty boxes without saying so. Any installed family covering
# JIS X 0208 will do; these are the usual ones on Linux, macOS and Windows.
cjk_fonts <- c("Noto Sans CJK JP", "Hiragino Sans", "Yu Gothic",
               "IPAexGothic", "Meiryo")

# Amounts are shown in millions of yen, which is the unit a Japanese report
# states its own statements in.
scale <- 1e6

# The point size of the text in a chart. A chart stands in a page of nine
# point text, so it is set a little smaller than the page around it.
chart_base_size <- 9

# Which documents carry a full set of annual statements. 120 is the annual
# securities report, the 有価証券報告書, and 130 its correction; see
# fincommons.financialreport.edinet.common.REPORT_TYPES. A quarterly or
# half-year report states the previous year end as its comparative, so
# reading the annual documents only is what keeps a figure of a year out of a
# filing that is not an annual report.
annual_doctypes <- c("120", "130")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The concepts the factsheet is built from
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# A concept is matched on its local name, the part after the colon, and not
# on the whole identifier. Three of the four prefixes a conversion uses are
# fixed -- jppfs_cor for the financial statements, jpcrp_cor for the
# disclosure ordinance, jpdei_cor for the document and entity information --
# but the fourth is built from the form and the filer's own EDINET code, and
# an element a filer created sits under that one. Fujitsu's operating profit
# is jpcrp030000-asr_E01766-000:OperatingProfitIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults:
# the name of an element of the five-year summary, carried by the filer's own
# prefix because the core taxonomy has no operating profit for an IFRS
# filer. Matching on the prefix as well would lose it, and lose it silently.
#
# A key may be given several names, in order of preference, because the name
# depends on the accounting standard the filer reports under and because the
# Japanese and the international lines of one statement are different lines:
#
#   Japan GAAP   NetSales, OrdinaryIncomeLoss, ProfitLossAttributableTo-
#                OwnersOfParent for a group and NetIncomeLoss for a parent
#   IFRS         RevenueIFRS, OperatingProfitIFRS, ProfitLossIFRS, and the
#                ...IFRS spelling of nearly everything else
#
# Every name below was read off a real conversion: Kojima's report for a
# filer that does not consolidate, Kanagawa Chuo Kotsu's for one that does
# under Japan GAAP, and Fujitsu's for one that does under IFRS. The coverage
# page names every key it looked for and did not find, so a name that is
# wrong for some other filer shows up as a named gap rather than a blank.
#
# `unit` is the unit class a key accepts, and a fact whose unit is not of
# that class is refused rather than shown. This is not belt and braces. In
# Fujitsu's own five-year summary the element named EquityToAssetRatioIFRS-
# SummaryOfBusinessResults carries 8094.70, 842.54, 952.76, 979.53, 1167.25
# with the unit JPYPerShares: the equity attributable to the owners of the
# parent per share, under the name of a ratio. A factsheet that trusted the
# name would print an equity ratio of 1,167 per cent, and the equity ratio is
# in that report all the same, under RatioOfOwnersEquityToGrossAssetsIFRS-
# SummaryOfBusinessResults, as 0.60.
#
#   money      JPY, and the amount is held in yen
#   shares     shares
#   pershare   JPYPerShares
#   ratio      pure, and the figure is a fraction rather than a percentage:
#              the filer states an equity ratio of 57.1 per cent as 0.571
#   count      pure, a number of people or of shareholders
#   years      pure, a length of time in years

# The five-year summary of the front matter, 主要な経営指標等の推移. This is
# the backbone of the factsheet and has no counterpart in the other two
# regimes: one report carries five years of it, so a lake holding a single
# annual report can show a five-year series.
summary_concepts <- list(
  revenue = c("NetSalesSummaryOfBusinessResults",
              "RevenueIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
              "OperatingRevenueSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  operating_profit = c("OperatingProfitIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
                       "OperatingIncomeLossSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  # 経常利益. The line between the operating result and the pre-tax result
  # of a Japanese statement, and the one a Japanese reader looks at first.
  # There is nothing to map it to under IFRS, where the pre-tax result
  # stands in its place.
  ordinary_income = c("OrdinaryIncomeLossSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  pretax = c("ProfitLossBeforeTaxIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  # The result attributable to the owners of the parent for a group, and the
  # result of the company for a filer that does not consolidate.
  profit = c("ProfitLossAttributableToOwnersOfParentIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
             "ProfitLossAttributableToOwnersOfParentSummaryOfBusinessResults",
             "NetIncomeLossSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  profit_group = c("ProfitLossIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  comprehensive_income = c("ComprehensiveIncomeIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
                           "ComprehensiveIncomeSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  equity = c("EquityAttributableToOwnersOfParentIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
             "NetAssetsSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  assets = c("TotalAssetsIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
             "TotalAssetsSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  capital_stock = c("CapitalStockSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  shares_issued = c("TotalNumberOfIssuedSharesSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  # The second name is the one an IFRS filer tags its equity per share
  # under, and it is the name of a ratio. Fujitsu states 1,167.25 there with
  # the unit JPYPerShares beside an equity of 2,024,915 million and 1,739.78
  # million shares, which is the equity per share and not a ratio of
  # anything. The same element therefore serves two keys and the unit
  # decides which: refused for the equity ratio, which wants a pure number,
  # and taken here, which wants an amount per share.
  equity_per_share = c("NetAssetsPerShareSummaryOfBusinessResults",
                       "EquityToAssetRatioIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  eps_basic = c("BasicEarningsLossPerShareIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
                "BasicEarningsLossPerShareSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  eps_diluted = c("DilutedEarningsLossPerShareIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
                  "DilutedEarningsPerShareSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  dividend_per_share = c("DividendPaidPerShareSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  interim_dividend_per_share = c("InterimDividendPaidPerShareSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  # 自己資本比率. The ratio, and not the per-share figure some filers tag
  # under the second of these names; the unit class is what tells them apart.
  equity_ratio = c("RatioOfOwnersEquityToGrossAssetsIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
                   "EquityToAssetRatioIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
                   "EquityToAssetRatioSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  roe = c("RateOfReturnOnEquityIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
          "RateOfReturnOnEquitySummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  payout_ratio = c("PayoutRatioSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  # 株価収益率. The one market figure in this document, and it is the
  # filer's own statement rather than a price fetched from anywhere.
  per = c("PriceEarningsRatioIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
          "PriceEarningsRatioSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  operating_cash_flow = c("CashFlowsFromUsedInOperatingActivitiesIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
                          "NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  investing_cash_flow = c("CashFlowsFromUsedInInvestingActivitiesIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
                          "NetCashProvidedByUsedInInvestingActivitiesSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  financing_cash_flow = c("CashFlowsFromUsedInFinancingActivitiesIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
                          "NetCashProvidedByUsedInFinancingActivitiesSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  cash = c("CashAndCashEquivalentsIFRSSummaryOfBusinessResults",
           "CashAndCashEquivalentsSummaryOfBusinessResults"),
  # Not a ...SummaryOfBusinessResults element, though it stands in the same
  # table of the report: the employee count of the summary is tagged under
  # the plain element, with five years of contexts.
  employees = c("NumberOfEmployees"),
  temporary_workers = c("AverageNumberOfTemporaryWorkers"),
  # 株主総利回り and the index it is set against, five years of each. The
  # filer states both; neither is computed here.
  tsr = c("TotalShareholderReturn"),
  tsr_index = c("TotalReturnOnSharePriceIndex")
)

summary_units <- c(
  revenue = "money", operating_profit = "money", ordinary_income = "money",
  pretax = "money", profit = "money", profit_group = "money",
  comprehensive_income = "money", equity = "money",
  assets = "money", capital_stock = "money", shares_issued = "shares",
  equity_per_share = "pershare", eps_basic = "pershare",
  eps_diluted = "pershare", dividend_per_share = "pershare",
  interim_dividend_per_share = "pershare", equity_ratio = "ratio",
  roe = "ratio", payout_ratio = "ratio", per = "ratio",
  operating_cash_flow = "money", investing_cash_flow = "money",
  financing_cash_flow = "money", cash = "money", employees = "count",
  temporary_workers = "count", tsr = "ratio", tsr_index = "ratio"
)

# The statements themselves, from the financial statements taxonomy. A report
# states two years of these -- the year and its comparative -- so the tables
# built from them are narrower than the five-year summary above, and
# deliberately so: a column of dashes for the years no statement covers would
# say less than a table that covers the years it has.
#
# The signs are as the statement presents them and are not flipped here. A
# Japanese conversion carries a deduction of the profit and loss account as a
# positive amount -- the cost of sales, the selling expenses, the tax -- and
# an outflow of the cash flow statement as a negative one, the purchase of
# property plant and equipment arriving as -1,939 million. See `sign` in the
# lines of the statements further down for where a table turns one round.
# The consolidated statements of an IFRS filer are a taxonomy of their own,
# jpigp_cor, and its names are not the Japan GAAP names with a suffix: the
# cost of sales is CostOfSalesIFRS but the stock is InventoriesCAIFRS, the
# trade receivables TradeReceivables2CAIFRS, the current liabilities
# TotalCurrentLiabilitiesIFRS and the tax charge IncomeTaxExpenseIFRS. The
# cash flow is the sharpest of these: the investing line of a Japan GAAP
# statement is NetCashProvidedByUsedInInvestmentActivities and of an IFRS one
# NetCashProvidedByUsedInInvestingActivitiesIFRS, Investment against
# Investing, with the five-year summary spelling it Investing for both. All
# three are read off real conversions.
statement_concepts <- list(
  # Profit and loss
  revenue = c("NetSales", "RevenueIFRS", "OperatingRevenue"),
  # A trading company builds its cost of sales up from the opening stock, the
  # purchases and the closing stock and states no 売上原価 total; Kojima
  # states 商品売上原価 instead, which is the same line of the same statement.
  cost_of_sales = c("CostOfSales", "CostOfGoodsSold", "CostOfSalesIFRS"),
  gross_profit = c("GrossProfit", "GrossProfitIFRS"),
  sgna = c("SellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpenses",
           "SellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpensesIFRS"),
  rnd = c("ResearchAndDevelopmentExpensesResearchAndDevelopmentActivities"),
  operating_income = c("OperatingIncome", "OperatingProfitLossIFRS"),
  nonoperating_income = c("NonOperatingIncome"),
  nonoperating_expenses = c("NonOperatingExpenses"),
  ordinary_income = c("OrdinaryIncome"),
  extraordinary_income = c("ExtraordinaryIncome"),
  extraordinary_loss = c("ExtraordinaryLoss"),
  # For an IFRS filer the element names the result before tax of the
  # continuing operations, which is what the statement presents: Fujitsu
  # states 409,034 million there and 146,908 million of pre-tax result from
  # operations it discontinued, and the two are not added up by the report.
  pretax = c("IncomeBeforeIncomeTaxes", "ProfitLossBeforeTaxIFRS"),
  pretax_discontinued = c("ProfitLossBeforeTaxFromDiscontinuedOperationsIFRS"),
  income_taxes = c("IncomeTaxes", "IncomeTaxExpenseIFRS"),
  income_taxes_current = c("IncomeTaxesCurrent"),
  income_taxes_deferred = c("IncomeTaxesDeferred"),
  profit_group = c("ProfitLoss", "ProfitLossIFRS"),
  profit_nci = c("ProfitLossAttributableToNonControllingInterests",
                 "ProfitLossAttributableToNonControllingInterestsIFRS"),
  profit = c("ProfitLossAttributableToOwnersOfParent",
             "ProfitLossAttributableToOwnersOfParentIFRS"),
  other_comprehensive_income = c("OtherComprehensiveIncome",
                                 "OtherComprehensiveIncomeIFRS"),
  comprehensive_income = c("ComprehensiveIncome", "ComprehensiveIncomeIFRS"),

  # Balance sheet
  assets = c("Assets", "AssetsIFRS"),
  current_assets = c("CurrentAssets", "CurrentAssetsIFRS"),
  noncurrent_assets = c("NoncurrentAssets", "NonCurrentAssetsIFRS"),
  equity_method = c("InvestmentsAccountedForUsingEquityMethodIFRS"),
  cash_and_deposits = c("CashAndDeposits", "CashAndCashEquivalentsIFRS"),
  # Receivables, inventories, payables and debt are summed from their
  # components further down rather than read from a total, because a Japanese
  # balance sheet subtotals none of the four. It lists 商品, 製品, 原材料及び
  # 貯蔵品 and 仕掛品 as separate lines and states no stock figure over them,
  # which is why a factsheet looking for an Inventories element finds nothing
  # and puts a retailer's whole stock into the residual: Kojima's 37,874
  # million of merchandise would sit in "other current assets" and the line
  # the reader wants would be a dash.
  receivable_notes = c("NotesReceivableTrade"),
  receivable_accounts = c("AccountsReceivableTrade"),
  receivable_both = c("NotesAndAccountsReceivableTradeAndContractAssets",
                      "NotesAndAccountsReceivableTrade",
                      "TradeReceivables2CAIFRS"),
  contract_assets = c("ContractAssets"),
  inventory_merchandise = c("Merchandise", "MerchandiseAndFinishedGoods",
                            "FinishedGoods"),
  inventory_work_in_process = c("WorkInProcess"),
  inventory_materials = c("RawMaterialsAndSupplies", "RawMaterials",
                          "Supplies"),
  inventory_total = c("Inventories", "InventoriesCAIFRS"),
  ppe = c("PropertyPlantAndEquipment", "PropertyPlantAndEquipmentIFRS"),
  intangibles = c("IntangibleAssets", "IntangibleAssetsIFRS"),
  goodwill = c("Goodwill", "GoodwillIFRS"),
  investments = c("InvestmentsAndOtherAssets"),
  liabilities = c("Liabilities", "LiabilitiesIFRS"),
  current_liabilities = c("CurrentLiabilities", "TotalCurrentLiabilitiesIFRS"),
  noncurrent_liabilities = c("NoncurrentLiabilities",
                             "TotalNonCurrentLiabilitiesIFRS"),
  payable_notes = c("NotesPayableTrade"),
  payable_accounts = c("AccountsPayableTrade"),
  payable_both = c("NotesAndAccountsPayableTrade", "TradePayables2CLIFRS"),
  short_term_loans = c("ShortTermLoansPayable",
                       "ShortTermBorrowingsCurrentPortionOfLongTermDebtAndLeaseLiabilitiesIFRS"),
  commercial_papers = c("CommercialPapers"),
  current_portion_long_term = c("CurrentPortionOfLongTermLoansPayable"),
  current_portion_bonds = c("CurrentPortionOfBonds"),
  long_term_loans = c("LongTermLoansPayable",
                      "LongTermDebtAndLeaseObligationsNCLIFRS"),
  bonds = c("BondsPayable"),
  lease_obligations = c("LeaseObligationsCL", "LeaseObligationsCLOther"),
  lease_obligations_noncurrent = c("LeaseObligationsNCL",
                                   "LeaseObligationsNCLOther"),
  net_assets = c("NetAssets", "EquityIFRS"),
  shareholders_equity = c("ShareholdersEquity",
                          "EquityAttributableToOwnersOfParentIFRS"),
  share_capital = c("CapitalStock", "ShareCapitalIFRS"),
  capital_surplus = c("CapitalSurplus", "CapitalSurplusIFRS"),
  retained_earnings = c("RetainedEarnings", "RetainedEarningsIFRS"),
  treasury_stock = c("TreasuryStock", "TreasurySharesIFRS"),
  valuation_adjustments = c("ValuationAndTranslationAdjustments",
                            "OtherComponentsOfEquityIFRS"),
  subscription_rights = c("SubscriptionRightsToShares"),
  nci = c("NonControllingInterests", "NonControllingInterestsIFRS"),
  liabilities_and_net_assets = c("LiabilitiesAndNetAssets",
                                 "LiabilitiesAndEquityIFRS"),

  # Cash flow. The investing line is spelled with Investment and not with
  # Investing, where the operating and the financing lines are spelled with
  # Activities; the five-year summary spells all three with Investing. Both
  # spellings are read off real conversions and neither is a typo here.
  operating_cash_flow = c("NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities",
                          "NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivitiesIFRS"),
  investing_cash_flow = c("NetCashProvidedByUsedInInvestmentActivities",
                          "NetCashProvidedByUsedInInvestingActivities",
                          "NetCashProvidedByUsedInInvestingActivitiesIFRS"),
  financing_cash_flow = c("NetCashProvidedByUsedInFinancingActivities",
                          "NetCashProvidedByUsedInFinancingActivitiesIFRS"),
  depreciation = c("DepreciationAndAmortizationOpeCF",
                   "DepreciationAndAmortizationOperatingExpensesIFRS"),
  capex_cash = c("PurchaseOfPropertyPlantAndEquipmentInvCF",
                 "PurchaseOfPropertyPlantAndEquipmentAndIntangibleAssetsInvCFIFRS"),
  dividends_paid = c("CashDividendsPaidFinCF",
                     "DividendsPaidToOwnersOfParentFinCFIFRS"),
  cash_end = c("CashAndCashEquivalents", "CashAndCashEquivalentsIFRS")
)

statement_units <- setNames(rep("money", length(statement_concepts)),
                            names(statement_concepts))

# What the filer says about itself and about its holders. These are facts of
# the latest report and of no period of the statements, so each is taken at
# the latest instant it is stated for.
profile_concepts <- list(
  name_ja = c("FilerNameInJapaneseDEI"),
  name_en = c("FilerNameInEnglishDEI"),
  standards = c("AccountingStandardsDEI"),
  consolidated_flag = c("WhetherConsolidatedFinancialStatementsArePreparedDEI"),
  form = c("DocumentTypeDEI"),
  ordinance = c("CabinetOfficeOrdinanceDEI"),
  period_type = c("TypeOfCurrentPeriodDEI"),
  amended = c("AmendmentFlagDEI"),
  security_code = c("SecurityCodeDEI"),
  submissions = c("NumberOfSubmissionDEI")
)

# The workforce of the parent company, which the ordinance asks for and which
# neither of the other two regimes has anything like.
workforce_concepts <- list(
  average_age = c("AverageAgeYearsInformationAboutReportingCompanyInformationAboutEmployees"),
  average_service = c("AverageLengthOfServiceYearsInformationAboutReportingCompanyInformationAboutEmployees"),
  average_salary = c("AverageAnnualSalaryInformationAboutReportingCompanyInformationAboutEmployees")
)
workforce_units <- c(average_age = "years", average_service = "years",
                     average_salary = "money")

# The holders of the shares: the structure by class of investor, and the ten
# largest by name.
# Facts of the report that are not figures of the accounts, and do not carry
# the dimension of a consolidation basis: see `member = "any"` below.
stated_concepts <- list(
  shareholders_total = c("NumberOfShareholdersTotal"),
  unit_shares = c("NumberOfSharesConstitutingOneUnit"),
  dividends_total = c("TotalAmountOfDividendsDividendsOfSurplus"),
  # 設備投資額, the capital expenditure as the filer states it in its review
  # of the year. It is not the purchase of property, plant and equipment of
  # the cash flow statement and the two usually differ: this one is what was
  # committed and that one what was paid.
  stated_capex = c("CapitalExpendituresOverviewOfCapitalExpendituresEtc")
)
stated_units <- c(shareholders_total = "count", unit_shares = "shares",
                  dividends_total = "money", stated_capex = "money")

# The classes of investor the ordinance names, in the order its table puts
# them. The share of each is tagged as a fraction under the class's own
# element rather than against a dimension.
holder_classes <- c(
  "Government and local government" = "PercentageOfShareholdingsNationalAndLocalGovernment",
  "Financial institutions" = "PercentageOfShareholdingsFinancialInstitutions",
  "Securities firms" = "PercentageOfShareholdingsFinancialServiceProviders",
  "Other corporations" = "PercentageOfShareholdingsOtherCorporations",
  "Foreign corporations" = "PercentageOfShareholdingsForeignersOtherThanIndividuals",
  "Foreign individuals" = "PercentageOfShareholdingsForeignIndividuals",
  "Individuals and others" = "PercentageOfShareholdingsIndividualsAndOthers"
)

# You can adapt your corporate design in the sourced R-Skript. It is one file
# for the whole package, in the templates directory at the root of it, so
# that a factsheet of any regime looks like the others and a change to the
# design is made once rather than once per module. A copy beside this
# template wins over it, which is what lets a template taken out of the
# package carry a design of its own.
library(ggplot2)
design_file <- "r-corporate-design-functions-ggplot2.R"
design_path <- c(design_file, file.path("..", "..", "..", "templates", design_file))
design_path <- design_path[file.exists(design_path)]
if (length(design_path) == 0) {
  stop("The corporate design script ", design_file, " is neither beside this ",
       "template nor in the templates directory of the package.")
}
source(design_path[1])

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(yaml)
library(arrow)
```

```{r lake}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The Silver layer
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

yaml_paths <- read_yaml(config_path)
path_silver <- yaml_paths[["edinet"]][["silver"]]

# The Silver layer may name a schema in a catalogue rather than a directory,
# with the directory the tables are written to beside it. R reads files, so
# it takes the directory.
if (is.list(path_silver)) path_silver <- path_silver[["path"]]

# arrow reads every parquet file under a directory. A Delta table keeps the
# files it has replaced until it is vacuumed, and the table of facts replaces
# the partition of a year on every run that collects a filing again, so a
# Delta table read this way counts a fact once for every time it was
# written. The factsheet therefore refuses one rather than show those sums.
for (table in c("filings", "facts")) {
  if (dir.exists(file.path(path_silver, table, "_delta_log"))) {
    stop("The ", table, " table of the edinet module is a Delta table, ",
         "which this template does not read. Write the Silver layer as ",
         "parquet, or read the table through Spark.")
  }
}

if (!grepl("^E[0-9]{5}$", filer_edinet_code)) {
  stop("The filer is named by its EDINET code, the letter E and five ",
       "digits: ", filer_edinet_code, " is not one. Kojima is E03270, and 7513 ",
       "is its securities code rather than its EDINET code.")
}

filings_all <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "filings")) %>%
  filter(edinet_code == filer_edinet_code) %>%
  collect()

if (nrow(filings_all) == 0) {
  stop("The table of filings lists no filing of ", filer_edinet_code, ". Collect ",
       "the indexes of the days the filer submitted on with the edinet ",
       "pipeline first; the table of filings is built from the indexes and ",
       "an index covers one calendar day.")
}

# The annual securities reports of the filer, the original of each year
# first: a correction restates, and the figure of a year as it was reported
# is the figure of the report that was filed first. A withdrawn filing is
# left out altogether -- the agency marks it and the filer took it back.
annual_all <- filings_all %>%
  filter(doc_type %in% annual_doctypes, has_csv == "1",
         is.na(withdrawn) | withdrawn == "0",
         !is.na(period_end)) %>%
  arrange(period_end, submitted)

if (nrow(annual_all) == 0) {
  stop("The filer has no annual securities report with a conversion in the ",
       "Silver layer. The table of filings lists ", nrow(filings_all),
       " filing(s) of ", filer_edinet_code, ", of document types ",
       paste(sort(unique(filings_all$doc_type)), collapse = ", "),
       "; this factsheet reads ", paste(annual_doctypes, collapse = " and "),
       " with a conversion the agency published.")
}

# The periods the statements of the reports cover, and the reports that cover
# them. One report states its own year and the one before it, so a lake
# holding a single report covers two years of statements and five of the
# summary of the front matter.
annual <- annual_all %>%
  group_by(period_end) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(period_end) %>%
  slice_tail(n = n_years)

facts_all <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "facts")) %>%
  filter(edinet_code == filer_edinet_code, filing %in% annual_all$filing) %>%
  collect()

if (nrow(facts_all) == 0) {
  stop("The Silver layer holds no fact of any annual report of ",
       filer_edinet_code, ". The agency's conversion of the report has to be in ",
       "the Bronze layer for the facts to be read from it; a run of ",
       "update_edinet over the day the report was filed collects it.")
}

latest_filing <- tail(annual$filing, 1)
filers <- NULL
if (dir.exists(file.path(path_silver, "filers"))) {
  filers <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "filers")) %>%
    filter(edinet_code == filer_edinet_code) %>%
    collect()
  if (nrow(filers) == 0) filers <- NULL
}

# The local name of an element: what this factsheet matches on. The prefix is
# kept beside it, because whether a concept is the filer's own extension or
# the taxonomy's is read off the prefix and the coverage page says which.
facts_all <- facts_all %>%
  mutate(prefix = sub(":.*", "", concept),
         local = sub(".*:", "", concept),
         extension = !prefix %in% c("jppfs_cor", "jpcrp_cor", "jpdei_cor",
                                    "jpigp_cor", "jpctl_cor", "jpsps_cor",
                                    "jppsp_cor", "jpaud_cor"))
```

```{r consolidation}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Which set of accounts, and how the two are told apart
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# A Japanese annual report states the consolidated accounts without a
# dimension and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember. A filer
# that prepares consolidated statements therefore states each figure twice
# and a filer that does not states it once, under the member -- so a
# factsheet that simply required an empty dimension would be empty for every
# filer that does not consolidate, and one that simply took the first fact it
# found would mix the group and the parent in one column.
#
# What the filing itself says is the authority here. The document and entity
# information carries 連結決算の有無 as a flag, and it disagrees with the
# agency's own list of filers for Kojima: the list says the filer has
# consolidated accounts, the filing says it prepared none, and the filing is
# the thing the figures come from.
dei <- facts_all %>% filter(filing == latest_filing, prefix == "jpdei_cor")

dei_of <- function(key) {
  names <- profile_concepts[[key]]
  row <- dei %>% filter(local %in% names)
  if (nrow(row) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  value <- coalesce(row$text[1], as.character(row$value[1]))
  # The conversion writes a full-width dash where a field does not apply.
  if (is.na(value) || value == "―" || value == "－" ||
      value == "−" || trimws(value) == "-") NA_character_ else value
}

standards <- dei_of("standards")
consolidated_flag <- dei_of("consolidated_flag")
filer_name_ja <- coalesce(dei_of("name_ja"), annual$name[nrow(annual)])
filer_name_en <- dei_of("name_en")

# Whether the consolidated series exists at all is decided by the data and
# not by the flag alone: a flag that says one thing and a report that states
# another is a filing to look at rather than a reason to show an empty
# column. The consolidated series is the facts with no dimension; it is held
# to exist where the filing states a revenue or a total of assets under none.
has_group <- facts_all %>%
  filter(filing == latest_filing, is.na(dimensions),
         local %in% c(summary_concepts$revenue, summary_concepts$assets,
                      statement_concepts$revenue, statement_concepts$assets),
         !is.na(value)) %>%
  nrow() > 0

if (!consolidation %in% c("auto", "consolidated", "nonconsolidated")) {
  stop("consolidation is \"auto\", \"consolidated\" or \"nonconsolidated\", ",
       "not ", consolidation)
}

group_basis <- switch(consolidation,
                      auto = has_group,
                      consolidated = TRUE,
                      nonconsolidated = FALSE)

if (consolidation == "consolidated" && !has_group) {
  warning("The filer states no consolidated figure in its latest annual ",
          "report, so a factsheet on the consolidated basis is empty. Set ",
          "consolidation to \"auto\" or \"nonconsolidated\".")
}

# The dimension a figure of the chosen basis carries, and the one a figure of
# the other basis carries. A key for which the chosen basis states nothing
# falls back to the other and is marked, because a few lines of the summary
# are stated for the parent only however the filer reports: the capital
# stock, the number of shares issued, the dividend per share and the payout
# ratio are properties of the company and not of the group, and Kanagawa Chuo
# Kotsu and Fujitsu both state them under the member alone.
member_chosen <- if (group_basis) NA_character_ else "NonConsolidatedMember"
member_other <- if (group_basis) "NonConsolidatedMember" else NA_character_

# Which lines may be taken from the other basis, and it is a short list on
# purpose. A few figures of the summary are properties of the company and of
# nothing else -- its stated capital, the shares it has issued, the dividend
# it declared and the payout that dividend was, the return its own shares
# gave -- and a filer states them under the parent however it reports, so a
# consolidated factsheet that refused them would show a dash where the report
# shows a figure.
#
# Every other line stays on the basis chosen, and this matters most for an
# IFRS filer. Fujitsu reports its group under IFRS and its parent company
# under Japan GAAP, so the parent's 経常利益 is in the same report: an
# unrestricted fallback put 275,236 million of parent-company ordinary
# profit on the cover of a group factsheet whose revenue is 3,502,971
# million, a figure of a different company under a different standard, and
# nothing on the page said so. The ordinary result does not exist under IFRS
# and a dash is the right answer.
fallback_keys <- c("capital_stock", "shares_issued", "dividend_per_share",
                   "interim_dividend_per_share", "payout_ratio",
                   "tsr", "tsr_index",
                   "average_age", "average_service", "average_salary")

#: Whether the statements read are IFRS ones, which decides how the equity is
#: composed and which lines the profit and loss account has at all.
ifrs_basis <- !is.na(standards) && standards == "IFRS" && group_basis

basis_label <- if (group_basis) "Consolidated" else "Non-consolidated"
basis_label_ja <- if (group_basis) "連結" else "単体"

if (!is.na(standards) && !standards %in% c("Japan GAAP", "IFRS", "US GAAP")) {
  warning("The filing states its accounting standard as \"", standards,
          "\", which this factsheet has no concept list for. Most lines ",
          "will be a dash and the coverage page will name them.")
}
if (!is.na(standards) && standards == "US GAAP") {
  warning("The filer reports under US GAAP, for which this factsheet ",
          "carries no concept list: the elements below are those of the ",
          "Japanese financial statements taxonomy and of the IFRS spelling ",
          "of the five-year summary. Read the registrant through the sec ",
          "module where it also files with the Commission.")
}
```

```{r selection}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Choosing one fact per key and per period
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The unit classes, and what counts as one. A fact whose unit is not of the
# class its key expects is refused: see the note on Fujitsu's equity ratio
# among the concepts above for why this is not a formality.
unit_classes <- list(money = "JPY", shares = "shares",
                     pershare = "JPYPerShares", ratio = "pure",
                     count = "pure", years = "pure")

# A statement line, as against a breakdown of one. The statement of changes
# in equity tags the net assets once per component of equity, so Kojima's
# report states NetAssets under NonConsolidatedMember_CapitalStockMember,
# ..._RetainedEarningsMember and seven other members besides the total; a
# selection by element and period alone would take whichever of them came
# first. A line of a statement carries the dimension of its basis and nothing
# further, which is what this tests.
on_basis <- function(data, member) {
  if (identical(member, "any")) {
    data
  } else if (is.na(member)) {
    data %>% filter(is.na(dimensions))
  } else {
    data %>% filter(!is.na(dimensions), dimensions == member)
  }
}

# Not everything in a report is a figure of the accounts, and what is not
# does not follow the consolidation rule. The number of shareholders and the
# size of a share unit are tagged against the class of share --
# `OrdinaryShareMember` -- the dividend declared against the row of the
# resolution that declared it, and the capital expenditure against nothing at
# all. For those `member` is "any" and the dimension decides nothing; where
# several facts remain, the one carrying the fewest dimensions is the total
# and the others are its breakdown, so the shortest wins.
dimension_depth <- function(dimensions) {
  ifelse(is.na(dimensions), 0L,
         lengths(strsplit(dimensions, "_", fixed = TRUE)))
}

# Which report a period is taken from, and the order that decides it.
own_filing <- setNames(annual$filing, as.character(annual$period_end))
filed_at <- setNames(as.numeric(annual_all$submitted), annual_all$filing)

if (!basis %in% c("as-reported", "latest")) {
  stop("basis is \"as-reported\" or \"latest\", not ", basis)
}

# The facts a figure may be taken from. Under "as-reported" a period is read
# from its own report where the lake holds it; a year of the five-year
# summary whose own report is not in the lake has only the later report that
# states it, and that figure is marked.
direction <- if (basis == "latest") -1 else 1

# `pick` takes the concept lists above and returns one row per key and per
# period: the first name of the key the filer states, on the chosen basis
# where it states it there and on the other basis where it does not, from the
# report the basis points to, with the unit class enforced.
#
# `source_basis` says which of the two a figure came from and `source_filing`
# which report, so that the marks in the tables and the coverage page rest on
# the selection itself rather than on a second pass over the data.
pick <- function(concepts, units, data = facts_all, periods = NULL,
                 member = member_chosen, fallback = member_other) {
  # `name` and not `key`: inside a tibble() call a bare `key` would resolve
  # to the column of that name being built rather than to the argument.
  lookup <- bind_rows(lapply(names(concepts), function(name) {
    tibble(key = name, local = concepts[[name]],
           preference = seq_along(concepts[[name]]))
  }))

  candidates <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
    inner_join(lookup, by = "local", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    mutate(class = units[key],
           ok_unit = mapply(function(u, cl) {
             if (is.na(cl)) TRUE else identical(u, unit_classes[[cl]])
           }, unit, class))

  refused <<- bind_rows(refused, candidates %>% filter(!ok_unit) %>%
                          select("key", "concept", "unit", "class", "value"))
  candidates <- candidates %>% filter(ok_unit)

  if (!is.null(periods)) {
    candidates <- candidates %>% filter(prd_end %in% periods)
  }

  chosen <- bind_rows(
    on_basis(candidates, member) %>% mutate(source_basis = "chosen"),
    on_basis(candidates, fallback) %>%
      filter(key %in% fallback_keys) %>%
      mutate(source_basis = "other")
  )
  if (nrow(chosen) == 0) {
    return(tibble(key = character(), prd_end = as.Date(character()),
                  value = numeric(), source_basis = character(),
                  source_filing = character(), own = logical(),
                  held = logical(), superseded = logical(),
                  extension = logical()))
  }

  chosen %>%
    mutate(depth = dimension_depth(dimensions),
           held = as.character(prd_end) %in% names(own_filing),
           own = filing == coalesce(own_filing[as.character(prd_end)], ""),
           # A figure the year's own report would have given differently is
           # one thing; a year whose own report the lake does not hold at all
           # is another, and only the first is a restatement. The five-year
           # summary of one report states four years whose own reports may be
           # nowhere in the lake, and marking those as restated would say
           # something false about every one of them.
           superseded = held & !own,
           ord_filing = direction * coalesce(filed_at[filing], 0),
           ord_basis = if_else(source_basis == "chosen", 0L, 1L)) %>%
    # One row per key and period: the basis asked for before the other, then
    # the report the basis points to, then the first name of the key the
    # filer states.
    arrange(key, prd_end, ord_basis, ord_filing, preference, depth) %>%
    group_by(key, prd_end) %>%
    slice(1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select("key", "prd_end", "prd_start", "value", "unit", "label", "concept",
           "source_basis", "source_filing" = "filing", "own", "held",
           "superseded", "extension")
}

# What was refused for its unit, which the coverage page reports.
refused <- tibble()

# The Japanese label of an element, as the conversion states it beside it.
# The suffix the ordinance appends to every element of a table -- 、経営指標等
# for the five-year summary -- is dropped, the table saying it once in its
# own heading.
trim_label <- function(text, drop = NULL) {
  if (is.null(drop)) return(text)
  for (suffix in drop) text <- sub(paste0(suffix, "$"), "", text)
  text
}
```

```{r figures}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The two year axes
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# A Japanese annual report gives a long headline series and a short detailed
# one, and this factsheet keeps them apart rather than padding the short one
# out with dashes. The five-year summary of the front matter covers five
# years in one report; the statements cover the year and its comparative. So
# the tables of the summary are five columns wide from a single report and
# the tables of the statements two, and each says in its own heading which
# years it covers.
summary_facts <- pick(summary_concepts, summary_units)
statement_facts <- pick(statement_concepts, statement_units)
# The facts of the latest report that are not figures of the accounts, taken
# on whatever dimension they carry.
stated <- pick(stated_concepts, stated_units,
               data = facts_all %>% filter(filing == latest_filing),
               member = "any", fallback = "any")

count_of <- function(key) {
  value <- stated$value[stated$key == key]
  if (length(value) == 0) NA_real_ else tail(value, 1)
}

if (nrow(summary_facts) == 0 && nrow(statement_facts) == 0) {
  stop("No figure of the concept lists was found on the ",
       tolower(basis_label), " basis in any annual report of ", filer_edinet_code,
       ". The filing states its accounting standard as \"", standards,
       "\"; if that is not Japan GAAP or IFRS the concept lists do not fit ",
       "it.")
}

widen <- function(chosen, keys) {
  if (nrow(chosen) == 0) {
    out <- tibble(period_end = as.Date(character()))
  } else {
    out <- chosen %>%
      select("period_end" = "prd_end", "key", "value") %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = "key", values_from = "value") %>%
      arrange(period_end)
  }
  for (key in setdiff(keys, names(out))) out[[key]] <- NA_real_
  out
}

# The years of the summary, counted back from the latest the filer states.
summary_years_all <- sort(unique(summary_facts$prd_end))
summary_years_all <- tail(summary_years_all, n_years)
wide <- widen(summary_facts %>% filter(prd_end %in% summary_years_all),
              names(summary_concepts)) %>%
  filter(period_end %in% summary_years_all)

# The years the statements cover, which are the period ends of the reports
# read and the comparative of the earliest of them.
statement_years_all <- sort(unique(statement_facts$prd_end))
statement_years_all <- tail(statement_years_all, n_years + 1)
stmt <- widen(statement_facts %>% filter(prd_end %in% statement_years_all),
              names(statement_concepts)) %>%
  filter(period_end %in% statement_years_all)

# The name of a financial year. A Japanese filer names its years by their
# ordinal -- Kojima's report is of its 64th term, 第64期 -- and the ordinal is
# in the description of the filing rather than among the facts, so the year
# is named here by the calendar year it ends in, with the month where the
# filer does not close in March. A reader of Japanese accounts reads FY2026
# of a March filer as the year to 31 March 2026, which is what this gives.
year_name <- function(dates) {
  ifelse(is.na(dates), "–",
         ifelse(format(dates, "%m") == "03",
                paste0("fy", format(dates, "%Y")),
                paste0("fy", format(dates, "%Y"), " (", format(dates, "%b"),
                       ")")))
}
wide$year <- year_name(wide$period_end)
stmt$year <- year_name(stmt$period_end)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What the figures are turned into
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The ratios of the summary are the filer's own and arrive as fractions: an
# equity ratio of 57.1 per cent is stated as 0.571 with the unit `pure`.
# They are brought onto percentages here and are marked in the tables as the
# filer's own, so that they are not read as this factsheet's calculation.
# The price-earnings ratio and the total shareholder return are multiples
# rather than percentages and are left as they are.
wide <- wide %>%
  mutate(across(any_of(c("equity_ratio", "roe", "payout_ratio")),
                ~ .x * 100))

wide <- wide %>%
  mutate(
    # The result the five-year summary gives, whichever of the two lines the
    # filer states it under.
    profit_shown = coalesce(profit, profit_group),
    # The operating result, which a Japan GAAP summary does not carry: its
    # three lines are revenue, the ordinary result and the net result. It is
    # in the statements and the statement tables show it; here it is a dash
    # for a Japan GAAP filer and a figure for an IFRS one.
    margin_operating = 100 * operating_profit / revenue,
    margin_ordinary = 100 * ordinary_income / revenue,
    margin_net = 100 * profit_shown / revenue,
    # Three ratios of our own, beside three of the filer's own further down.
    # Each is marked in its table as a calculation and not as a statement.
    roa = 100 * profit_shown / ((assets + lag(assets)) / 2),
    asset_turnover = revenue / ((assets + lag(assets)) / 2),
    free_cash_flow = operating_cash_flow + investing_cash_flow,
    fcf_margin = 100 * (operating_cash_flow + investing_cash_flow) / revenue,
    cash_to_profit = operating_cash_flow / profit_shown,
    revenue_growth = 100 * (revenue / lag(revenue) - 1),
    ordinary_growth = 100 * (ordinary_income / lag(ordinary_income) - 1),
    profit_growth = 100 * (profit_shown / lag(profit_shown) - 1),
    equity_growth = 100 * (equity / lag(equity) - 1),
    dividend_total_per_share = dividend_per_share,
    # The dividend cover, which is the payout the other way up and is shown
    # beside the filer's own payout ratio.
    dividend_cover = eps_basic / dividend_per_share,
    # The issued share count as at each year end, and what it did. A Japanese
    # filer that splits its stock restates the per-share figures of its
    # five-year summary at its own discretion and not always for every year
    # of it: Fujitsu's report states 207.0, 207.0, 207.1, 2,071.1 and 1,739.8
    # million shares and earnings per share of 924.21, 110.76, 135.59, 120.93
    # and 254.83, which is four years restated onto the shares after the
    # ten-for-one split of October 2024 and the fifth left on the shares
    # before it. No factor is applied here for that reason -- dividing a
    # restated year by it would be wrong -- and the year the count moved is
    # named instead, so that a per-share series spanning a split is read as
    # one.
    share_ratio = shares_issued / lag(shares_issued)
  )

stmt <- stmt %>%
  mutate(
    # The cost of sales where the statement totals it, and what is left
    # between revenue and the gross result where it does not: a retailer
    # builds its cost of sales up from the opening stock, the purchases and
    # the closing stock, and Kojima's statement carries those three lines and
    # no total.
    cost_of_sales_shown = coalesce(cost_of_sales, revenue - gross_profit),
    gross_profit_shown = coalesce(gross_profit, revenue - cost_of_sales),
    # The four lines a Japanese balance sheet does not subtotal, summed from
    # the components the statement states. `..._both` is the line a filer
    # that presents notes and accounts together states, and it is taken
    # instead of the two separate ones rather than beside them.
    receivables = coalesce(receivable_both,
                           coalesce(receivable_notes, 0) +
                             coalesce(receivable_accounts, 0) +
                             coalesce(contract_assets, 0)),
    receivables = if_else(receivables == 0, NA_real_, receivables),
    inventories = coalesce(inventory_total,
                           coalesce(inventory_merchandise, 0) +
                             coalesce(inventory_work_in_process, 0) +
                             coalesce(inventory_materials, 0)),
    inventories = if_else(inventories == 0, NA_real_, inventories),
    payables = coalesce(payable_both,
                        coalesce(payable_notes, 0) +
                          coalesce(payable_accounts, 0)),
    payables = if_else(payables == 0, NA_real_, payables),
    net_nonoperating = coalesce(nonoperating_income, 0) -
      coalesce(nonoperating_expenses, 0),
    net_extraordinary = coalesce(extraordinary_income, 0) -
      coalesce(extraordinary_loss, 0),
    profit_shown = coalesce(profit, profit_group),
    # Interest-bearing debt as the statement's own lines add up to it. A
    # Japanese balance sheet has no total for it and a filer tags no such
    # concept, so this is a sum of the lines the table names and nothing
    # wider.
    debt = coalesce(short_term_loans, 0) +
      coalesce(commercial_papers, 0) +
      coalesce(current_portion_long_term, 0) +
      coalesce(current_portion_bonds, 0) +
      coalesce(long_term_loans, 0) + coalesce(bonds, 0) +
      coalesce(lease_obligations, 0) +
      coalesce(lease_obligations_noncurrent, 0),
    debt = if_else(debt == 0, NA_real_, debt),
    net_debt = coalesce(debt, 0) - coalesce(cash_and_deposits, 0),
    # The equity of the holders of the parent's shares, which is the net
    # assets less what belongs to others. A filer that does not consolidate
    # has no non-controlling interest and the two are the same.
    equity_parent = net_assets - coalesce(nci, 0) -
      coalesce(subscription_rights, 0),
    # What the components of equity should add up to, which is not the same
    # question under the two standards. A Japan GAAP balance sheet presents
    # 株主資本 and 評価・換算差額等 as two parts of the net assets; an IFRS
    # one presents 親会社の所有者に帰属する持分, which already contains the
    # other components of equity, and only the non-controlling interests
    # stand outside it. Fujitsu's parent equity of 2,024,915 million and its
    # other components of 73,239 million are not two things to add.
    equity_component_sum = if (ifrs_basis) {
      coalesce(shareholders_equity, 0) + coalesce(nci, 0)
    } else {
      coalesce(shareholders_equity, 0) + coalesce(valuation_adjustments, 0) +
        coalesce(subscription_rights, 0) + coalesce(nci, 0)
    },
    other_current_assets = current_assets - coalesce(cash_and_deposits, 0) -
      coalesce(receivables, 0) - coalesce(inventories, 0),
    # An IFRS statement of financial position subtotals its current
    # liabilities and leaves the non-current side to be read as the
    # remainder, which is what is done here where no total is stated. The
    # same is true of the non-current assets of a Japan GAAP statement that
    # states only the current ones.
    noncurrent_liabilities = coalesce(noncurrent_liabilities,
                                      liabilities - current_liabilities),
    noncurrent_assets = coalesce(noncurrent_assets,
                                 assets - current_assets),
    other_noncurrent_assets = noncurrent_assets - coalesce(ppe, 0) -
      coalesce(goodwill, 0) - coalesce(intangibles, 0) -
      coalesce(investments, 0) - coalesce(equity_method, 0),
    other_current_liabilities = current_liabilities -
      coalesce(payables, 0) - coalesce(short_term_loans, 0) -
      coalesce(commercial_papers, 0) -
      coalesce(current_portion_long_term, 0) -
      coalesce(current_portion_bonds, 0) -
      coalesce(lease_obligations, 0),
    other_noncurrent_liabilities = noncurrent_liabilities -
      coalesce(long_term_loans, 0) - coalesce(bonds, 0) -
      coalesce(lease_obligations_noncurrent, 0),
    ebitda = operating_income + coalesce(depreciation, 0),
    margin_gross = 100 * gross_profit_shown / revenue,
    margin_operating = 100 * operating_income / revenue,
    margin_ordinary = 100 * ordinary_income / revenue,
    margin_pretax = 100 * pretax / revenue,
    margin_net = 100 * profit_shown / revenue,
    sgna_share = 100 * sgna / revenue,
    rnd_share = 100 * rnd / revenue,
    cost_share = 100 * cost_of_sales_shown / revenue,
    effective_tax_rate = 100 * income_taxes / pretax,
    equity_ratio = 100 * equity_parent / assets,
    gearing = 100 * net_debt / equity_parent,
    net_debt_to_ebitda = net_debt / ebitda,
    current_ratio = current_assets / current_liabilities,
    quick_ratio = (current_assets - coalesce(inventories, 0)) /
      current_liabilities,
    inventory_days = 365 * inventories / cost_of_sales_shown,
    receivable_days = 365 * receivables / revenue,
    payable_days = 365 * payables / cost_of_sales_shown,
    free_cash_flow = operating_cash_flow + investing_cash_flow,
    capex = -coalesce(capex_cash, 0),
    capex_to_revenue = 100 * (-coalesce(capex_cash, 0)) / revenue,
    capex_to_depreciation = (-coalesce(capex_cash, 0)) / depreciation,
    cash_conversion = 100 * operating_cash_flow / ebitda,
    roe = 100 * profit_shown / ((equity_parent + lag(equity_parent)) / 2),
    roa = 100 * profit_shown / ((assets + lag(assets)) / 2)
  )

# The years actually shown. For the statements the extra year behind them has
# served the returns, which put a flow of a year against the average of the
# balances at its start and its end.
shown <- wide
n_shown <- nrow(shown)
years <- shown$year
max_date <- max(c(shown$period_end, stmt$period_end))

shown_stmt <- stmt %>% slice_tail(n = max(1, nrow(stmt) - 1))
if (nrow(stmt) == 1) shown_stmt <- stmt
n_stmt <- nrow(shown_stmt)
stmt_years <- shown_stmt$year

cur <- if (n_shown > 0) as.list(tail(shown, 1)) else list()
cur_stmt <- if (n_stmt > 0) as.list(tail(shown_stmt, 1)) else list()
```

```{r formats}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Writing numbers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  # A figure that rounds to nothing is written as nothing rather than as a
  # signed nothing: an amount of minus four hundred thousand is 0 in a
  # column of millions, not -0.
  x <- ifelse(!is.na(x) & abs(x) < 0.5 / 10^digits, 0, x)
  ifelse(is.na(x) | is.infinite(x), "–",
         formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",",
                 decimal.mark = "."))
}

# A growth rate or a change carries its sign, so that a fall is visible
# without reading the column beside it.
fmt_signed <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  ifelse(is.na(x) | is.infinite(x), "–",
         paste0(ifelse(x > 0, "+", ""),
                formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",",
                        decimal.mark = ".")))
}

# A caption wider than the figure is clipped rather than wrapped, so it is
# broken into lines once here.
wrap_caption <- function(text, width = 125) {
  paste(strwrap(text, width = width), collapse = "\n")
}

source_caption <- caption_corporate_design(
  source = paste0("Annual securities report as converted by the Financial ",
                  "Services Agency, EDINET. ", basis_label, " basis."),
  last = format(max_date, "%d %b %Y"),
  lang = "en")

amount_label <- "JPY million"

# The x-axis of a chart of the summary has one break per financial year,
# named as the tables name it.
year_labels <- setNames(shown$year, as.character(shown$period_end))
scale_x_years <- function(...) {
  scale_x_date(expand = c(.02, 0), breaks = shown$period_end,
               labels = function(d) year_labels[as.character(d)], ...)
}

# Escape what typst reads as its own syntax, for the text that goes into the
# raw blocks of the cover and of the running head.
# It is named apart from typst_string of the design script, which also puts
# the quotes around the text and which the title of the document and its
# coloured tables call: a function of the same name here would replace it.
typst_escape <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("\\\\", "\\\\\\\\", x)
  gsub("\"", "\\\\\"", x)
}
```

```{r lines}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The tables: one function for every table of the factsheet
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Every table is one row per line of a statement or per indicator and one
# column per financial year. `spec` describes the lines:
#
#   key      the column of the data the line reads, or "" for a heading
#   en       the English name this template gives the line
#   digits   the decimals shown
#   unit     "amount"  in millions of yen, the figures being held in yen
#            "raw"     as held, for a per-share amount or a multiple
#            "pct"     a percentage, which the key already holds
#            "signed"  a percentage or a change, written with its sign
#            "shares"  a share count, in millions
#            "count"   a number of people, as held
#            "years"   a length of time in years
#   sign     -1 for a line a table shows as the deduction it is, where the
#            conversion carries it as a positive amount
#   style    "" for an ordinary line, "total" for a sum, "head" for a
#            heading, "sub" for a line indented below the one above it
#
# Three marks may follow a label, and each says where the figure came from:
#
#   †   from a report other than the year's own, which can only happen
#       under the "latest" basis or for a year of the five-year summary
#       whose own report the lake does not hold
#   ‡   from the other consolidation basis, the chosen one stating nothing
#       for that line: the capital stock and the dividend per share are
#       parent-company figures however the filer reports
#   §   from a concept the filer created for its own report rather than from
#       the taxonomy
line_spec <- function(...) {
  spec <- tribble(...)
  if (!"sign" %in% names(spec)) spec$sign <- 1
  if (!"style" %in% names(spec)) spec$style <- ""
  spec
}

# Where each key's figures came from, over the years shown, which the marks
# and the coverage page both read.
provenance <- bind_rows(
  summary_facts %>% filter(prd_end %in% shown$period_end) %>%
    mutate(table = "summary"),
  statement_facts %>% filter(prd_end %in% shown_stmt$period_end) %>%
    mutate(table = "statements")
)

marks_of <- function(keys, table = NULL) {
  rows <- if (is.null(table)) provenance else
    provenance %>% filter(table == !!table)
  vapply(keys, function(key) {
    if (!nzchar(key)) return("")
    found <- rows %>% filter(key == !!key)
    if (nrow(found) == 0) return("")
    paste0(if (any(found$superseded)) "†" else "",
           if (any(found$source_basis == "other")) "‡" else "",
           if (any(found$extension)) "§" else "")
  }, character(1))
}

label_of <- function(spec, table = NULL) {
  if (labels == "en") return(spec$en)
  rows <- if (is.null(table)) provenance else
    provenance %>% filter(table == !!table)
  japanese <- vapply(spec$key, function(key) {
    if (!nzchar(key)) return(NA_character_)
    found <- rows %>% filter(key == !!key, !is.na(label))
    if (nrow(found) == 0) return(NA_character_)
    trim_label(found$label[1], c("、経営指標等", "、提出会社の状況、従業員の状況"))
  }, character(1))
  if (labels == "ja") {
    ifelse(is.na(japanese), spec$en, japanese)
  } else {
    ifelse(is.na(japanese), spec$en, paste0(spec$en, " · ", japanese))
  }
}

format_line <- function(values, unit, digits) {
  switch(unit,
         amount = fmt(values / scale, digits),
         shares = fmt(values / 1e6, digits),
         raw = fmt(values, digits),
         pct = fmt(values, digits),
         count = fmt(values, digits),
         years = fmt(values, digits),
         signed = fmt_signed(values, digits),
         fmt(values, digits))
}

render_lines <- function(spec, data = shown, unit_header = NULL,
                         cagr = FALSE, change = FALSE, table = NULL) {
  out <- tibble(item = label_of(spec, table))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(data))) {
    column <- character(nrow(spec))
    for (j in seq_len(nrow(spec))) {
      if (spec$style[j] == "head" || !nzchar(spec$key[j])) {
        column[j] <- ""
      } else if (!spec$key[j] %in% names(data)) {
        column[j] <- "–"
      } else {
        value <- data[[spec$key[j]]][i] * spec$sign[j]
        column[j] <- format_line(value, spec$unit[j], spec$digits[j])
      }
    }
    out[[data$year[i]]] <- column
  }

  # The change on the year before and the growth over the window, which only
  # an amount and a per-share figure are shown with: the change of a ratio is
  # read off the ratios themselves.
  countable <- c("amount", "raw", "shares", "count")
  if (change) {
    out[["Change, %"]] <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(spec)), function(j) {
      if (!nzchar(spec$key[j]) || !spec$unit[j] %in% countable) return("")
      if (!spec$key[j] %in% names(data)) return("–")
      v <- data[[spec$key[j]]]
      if (length(v) < 2 || is.na(v[length(v)]) || is.na(v[length(v) - 1]) ||
          v[length(v) - 1] == 0) return("–")
      # A percentage change is left out where either end of it is negative.
      # An investing cash flow that went from -3,016 to -1,433 is a smaller
      # outflow, and the arithmetic calls that -52.5 per cent; a reader of a
      # column of percentages takes a minus sign for a fall. The two figures
      # are in the columns beside it and say it without the ambiguity.
      if (v[length(v)] < 0 || v[length(v) - 1] < 0) return("·")
      fmt_signed((v[length(v)] / v[length(v) - 1] - 1) * 100, 1)
    }, character(1))
  }
  if (cagr) {
    n <- nrow(data)
    out[["CAGR, %"]] <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(spec)), function(j) {
      if (!nzchar(spec$key[j]) || !spec$unit[j] %in% countable) return("")
      if (!spec$key[j] %in% names(data) || n < 2) return("–")
      v <- data[[spec$key[j]]]
      if (is.na(v[1]) || is.na(v[n])) return("–")
      if (v[1] <= 0 || v[n] <= 0) return("·")
      fmt_signed(((v[n] / v[1])^(1 / (n - 1)) - 1) * 100, 1)
    }, character(1))
  }

  # The marks and the styles, which markdown carries into the table.
  out$item <- paste0(out$item, marks_of(spec$key, table))
  out$item <- ifelse(spec$style == "sub", paste0(" ", out$item), out$item)
  bold <- spec$style %in% c("total", "head")
  for (column in names(out)) {
    out[[column]] <- ifelse(bold & nzchar(out[[column]]),
                            paste0("**", out[[column]], "**"), out[[column]])
  }

  header <- c(if (is.null(unit_header)) "" else unit_header, names(out)[-1])
  knitr::kable(out, col.names = header,
               align = paste0("l", strrep("r", ncol(out) - 1)))
}
```

```{r charts}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The charts: one function for a stack, a group of bars and a set of lines
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Each takes the keys of the data to show and their labels, in the order they
# are to be read, and leaves the corporate design to the sourced script. The
# labels are the English ones whatever `labels` is set to: a chart is drawn
# by the graphics device in the font the design names, which covers no
# Japanese, and a Japanese label would be drawn as empty boxes.
#
# No series is told apart by its colour alone, so that a reader who does not
# see colour reads the chart as well as one who does (WCAG 2.2, 1.4.1): the
# lines differ by their line type as well, a group of bars is split into one
# panel per series, named above it, and every layer of the stack is named
# beside it.
chart_data <- function(keys, labels, scale_by = scale, data = shown) {
  present <- keys[keys %in% names(data)]
  labels <- labels[keys %in% names(data)]
  data %>%
    select(all_of(c("period_end", present))) %>%
    pivot_longer(-"period_end", names_to = "var") %>%
    mutate(value = value / scale_by,
           var = factor(var, levels = present,
                        labels = wrap_labels(labels, 34)))
}

# What a chart shows, as text: the alt text of its figure, which a screen
# reader reads in place of the picture. It names the kind of chart, the
# series, the unit and the years, then each series year by year with its
# highest and lowest year, which is what a sighted reader takes from a chart
# of five years.
chart_alt <- function(kind, keys, labels, unit, scale_by = scale, digits = 0,
                      data = shown, note = "") {
  present <- keys %in% names(data)
  if (!any(present) || nrow(data) == 0) {
    return(paste0(kind, " of ", paste(labels, collapse = ", "),
                  ": the reports read state none of it, so the chart is empty."))
  }
  year_of <- data$year
  series <- vapply(which(present), function(i) {
    v <- data[[keys[i]]] / scale_by
    if (all(is.na(v))) return(paste0(labels[i], ": not stated"))
    known <- !is.na(v)
    text <- paste0(year_of[known], " ", fmt(v[known], digits), collapse = ", ")
    extremes <- if (sum(known) > 2) paste0(
      "; highest in ", year_of[known][which.max(v[known])],
      ", lowest in ", year_of[known][which.min(v[known])]) else ""
    paste0(labels[i], ": ", text, extremes)
  }, character(1))
  absent <- if (any(!present)) paste0(" Not stated: ",
                                      paste(labels[!present], collapse = ", "),
                                      ".") else ""
  paste0(kind, " of ", paste(labels[present], collapse = ", "), ", in ", unit,
         ", financial years ", year_of[1], " to ", year_of[length(year_of)],
         ", ", basis_label, " basis", note, ". ", paste(series, collapse = ". "),
         ".", absent)
}

# A stack of the parts of a whole, each layer named beside the last bar and
# joined to it by a leader line, so that the legend is not the only key to
# the colours. Where layers lie close together their names are spread apart
# along the axis, the leader line still pointing to the layer itself.
chart_stacked <- function(keys, labels, subtitle = amount_label,
                          scale_by = scale, ncol = 2, data = shown,
                          width = 250) {
  long <- chart_data(keys, labels, scale_by, data)
  last <- long %>%
    filter(period_end == max(period_end), !is.na(value), value > 0) %>%
    # geom_col stacks the first level of the factor on top.
    arrange(desc(as.integer(var))) %>%
    mutate(top = cumsum(value), middle = top - value / 2)
  gap <- 0.09 * max(c(sum(last$value), 1))
  position <- last$middle
  for (i in seq_along(position)[-1]) {
    position[i] <- max(position[i], position[i - 1] + gap)
  }
  # Pushed up from the bottom, the names may run over the top of the stack;
  # they are pulled back down by as much as they overrun it.
  overrun <- max(0, max(c(position, 0)) - sum(last$value))
  last$label_y <- pmax(position - overrun, 0)
  x_bar <- max(long$period_end) + width / 2
  x_text <- max(long$period_end) + width / 2 + 120
  ggplot(long, aes(x = period_end, y = value, fill = var)) +
    geom_col(width = width) +
    geom_zeroline() +
    geom_segment(data = last, aes(x = x_bar, xend = x_text - 10,
                                  y = middle, yend = label_y),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = design_colours()[["ink_soft"]],
                 linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_text(data = last, aes(x = x_text, y = label_y, label = var),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, size = chart_base_size / 3.2,
              lineheight = 0.85, colour = design_colours()[["ink"]]) +
    scale_x_date(expand = expansion(mult = c(.02, 0.02)),
                 breaks = data$period_end,
                 labels = function(d) year_labels[as.character(d)]) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(min(long$period_end) - width / 2,
                             x_text + 700), clip = "off") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) fmt(x)) +
    scale_fill_stack(guide = "none") +
    labs(caption = wrap_caption(source_caption), subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size,
                           axis.title = element_blank())
}

# A group of bars, one panel per series, its name above it: the panels share
# one scale, so the bars of two series compare as they would side by side.
# The name tells the series apart, so the bars of every panel are in the one
# colour of the design that stands out most from the page.
chart_bars <- function(keys, labels, subtitle = amount_label,
                       scale_by = scale, digits = 0, ncol = 3, data = shown,
                       width = 240) {
  long <- chart_data(keys, labels, scale_by, data)
  panels <- nlevels(long$var) > 1
  g <- ggplot(long, aes(x = period_end, y = value)) +
    geom_col(width = width, fill = palette_corporate_design("cat", 1)) +
    geom_zeroline() +
    # A panel is a third of the width, and the name of a year is broken
    # before the month its year ends in so that the names do not overlap.
    scale_x_date(expand = c(.02, 0), breaks = shown$period_end,
                 labels = function(d) {
                   l <- year_labels[as.character(d)]
                   if (panels) sub(" (", "\n(", l, fixed = TRUE) else l
                 }) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) fmt(x, digits)) +
    labs(caption = wrap_caption(source_caption), subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size,
                           axis.title = element_blank())
  if (panels) g <- g + facet_wrap(~var, nrow = 1)
  g
}

# A set of lines, told apart by colour and by line type, with the key of
# both below the chart.
chart_lines <- function(keys, labels, subtitle = "%", scale_by = 1,
                        digits = 0, zero = TRUE, ncol = 3, data = shown) {
  g <- ggplot(chart_data(keys, labels, scale_by, data) %>%
                filter(!is.na(value)),
              aes(x = period_end, y = value, colour = var, linetype = var)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = linewidth_corporate_design) +
    geom_point(size = 1.4) +
    scale_x_years() +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) fmt(x, digits)) +
    scale_colour_accessible(name = NULL) +
    scale_linetype_accessible(name = NULL) +
    labs(caption = wrap_caption(source_caption), subtitle = subtitle) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = ncol), linetype = guide_legend(ncol = ncol)) +
    theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size,
                           axis.title = element_blank()) +
    theme(legend.key.width = grid::unit(2.2, "lines"))
  if (zero) g <- g + geom_zeroline()
  g
}

# The alt text of every chart of the factsheet, written here from the same
# keys and labels the chunks below draw.
alt_revenue <- chart_alt("Bar chart", "revenue", "Revenue", amount_label)
alt_profit <- chart_alt("Bar chart in two panels",
                        c("ordinary_income", "profit_shown"),
                        c("Ordinary profit", "Net profit"), amount_label)
alt_cash_flows <- chart_alt("Bar chart in three panels",
                            c("operating_cash_flow", "investing_cash_flow",
                              "financing_cash_flow"),
                            c("Operating cash flow", "Investing cash flow",
                              "Financing cash flow"), amount_label)
alt_margins <- chart_alt("Line chart", c("margin_ordinary", "margin_net", "roe"),
                         c("Ordinary margin", "Net margin", "Return on equity"),
                         "per cent", scale_by = 1, digits = 1)
asset_keys <- c("cash_and_deposits", "receivables", "inventories",
                "other_current_assets", "ppe", "goodwill", "intangibles",
                "investments", "equity_method", "other_noncurrent_assets")
asset_labels <- c("Cash and deposits", "Trade receivables", "Inventories",
                  "Other current", "Property, plant and equipment", "Goodwill",
                  "Intangibles", "Investments", "Equity-method associates",
                  "Other non-current")
alt_assets <- chart_alt("Stacked bar chart, one bar a year making up total assets,",
                        asset_keys, asset_labels, amount_label, data = shown_stmt,
                        note = "; each part is named beside the last bar")
alt_cash_to_profit <- chart_alt("Line chart", "cash_to_profit",
                                "Operating cash flow to net profit", "multiples",
                                scale_by = 1, digits = 1)
alt_workforce <- chart_alt("Bar chart in two panels",
                           c("employees", "temporary_workers"),
                           c("Employees", "Temporary workers"), "people",
                           scale_by = 1)
alt_tsr <- chart_alt("Line chart", c("tsr", "tsr_index"),
                     c("Total shareholder return", "Comparison index"),
                     "cumulative multiples of the value at the start",
                     scale_by = 1, digits = 2)
```

```{r title, results='asis'}
# The title of the document, which a screen reader announces and without
# which typst refuses to write a PDF/UA document: the filer and the years,
```
