```{r cover, results='asis'}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The cover and the running head
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The filer and the period are read from the filings, so the cover is written
# as typst rather than set in the front matter. A value goes in as a typst
# string, which keeps a name with a hash or an underscore in it from being
# read as typst's own syntax.
ts <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x)) x <- "–"
  paste0("\"", typst_escape(as.character(x)), "\"")
}

# A column of the cover: a label and a value per row.
typst_kv <- function(items) {
  rows <- vapply(seq_along(items), function(i) {
    paste0("  text(size: 7.5pt, fill: soft, ", ts(names(items)[i]), "),\n",
           "  text(size: 8.5pt, ", ts(items[[i]]), "),")
  }, character(1))
  paste0("#grid(columns: (3.5cm, 1fr), row-gutter: 5.5pt, column-gutter: 6pt,\n",
         paste(rows, collapse = "\n"), "\n)")
}

subtitle_name <- if (!is.na(filer_name_ja) &&
                     !identical(filer_name_ja, display_name))
  filer_name_ja else NA_character_

identity_items <- list()
identity_items[["EDINET code"]] <- filer_edinet_code
identity_items[["Securities code"]] <- coalesce(dei_of("security_code"),
                                                annual$sec_code[nrow(annual)],
                                                "–")
identity_items[["Corporate number"]] <- coalesce(annual$jcn[nrow(annual)], "–")
identity_items[["Industry"]] <- coalesce(filer_row$industry, "–")
identity_items[["Accounting standard"]] <- coalesce(standards, "–")
identity_items[["Basis of these figures"]] <-
  paste0(basis_label, " (", basis_label_ja, ")")
identity_items[["Financial year ends"]] <- coalesce(filer_row$year_end,
                                                    format(max_date, "%d %B"))
identity_items[["Latest report"]] <- paste(
  "filed", format(as.Date(tail(annual$submitted, 1)), "%d %b %Y"))
identity_items[["Reports read"]] <- as.character(nrow(annual))

summary_items <- list()
summary_items[["Revenue"]] <- paste(fmt(cur$revenue / scale), amount_label)
# The ordinary result for a Japan GAAP filer and the pre-tax result for an
# IFRS one, which is the line standing in its place: naming the row after
# whichever the filer states keeps a dash off the cover and keeps the other
# standard's line out of it.
if (!is.null(cur$ordinary_income) && !is.na(cur$ordinary_income)) {
  summary_items[["Ordinary result"]] <- paste(
    fmt(cur$ordinary_income / scale), amount_label)
} else {
  summary_items[["Result before tax"]] <- paste(fmt(cur$pretax / scale),
                                                amount_label)
}
summary_items[["Net result"]] <- paste(fmt(cur$profit_shown / scale),
                                       amount_label)
summary_items[["Net margin"]] <- paste0(fmt(cur$margin_net, 1), " %")
summary_items[["Total assets"]] <- paste(fmt(cur$assets / scale), amount_label)
summary_items[["Equity ratio"]] <- paste0(fmt(cur$equity_ratio, 1), " %")
summary_items[["Return on equity"]] <- paste0(fmt(cur$roe, 1), " %")
summary_items[["Earnings per share"]] <- paste(fmt(cur$eps_basic, 2), "JPY")

notice <- paste(
  "Compiled from the filer's own annual securities reports as the Financial",
  "Services Agency converted them, published through EDINET. Every figure is",
  "a fact of a report or is derived from facts of the same report; no market",
  "data, estimate or forecast is used, the price-earnings ratio and the total",
  "shareholder return being the filer's own statements in its five-year",
  "summary. Where a ratio is the filer's own it is marked as such, and the",
  "remaining indicators are computed by this factsheet and are not the",
  "filer's own measures. The periods of the two most recent years are the",
  "dates the filing states about itself and those of the earlier years are",
  "shifted by whole years from them; see the notes on the figures. This",
  "document is produced by a template of the open-source project fincommons",
  "and the filer is an example: it is a summary of published accounts, given",
  "without warranty as to correctness or completeness, without any",
  "association with the filer, and it is not investment advice. The",
  "disclaimer on the last page applies.")

cat("```{=typst}\n")
# The page is set in the font the design names, which has no Japanese
# characters in it. A list gives typst a fallback to reach for them, and
# without one it sets them as empty boxes and says nothing.
cat("#set text(font: (\"Segoe UI\", ",
    paste(vapply(cjk_fonts, ts, character(1)), collapse = ", "), "))\n",
    sep = "")
cat("#set page(numbering: none)\n")
cat("#let ink = rgb(\"#22282E\")\n")
cat("#let soft = rgb(\"#5C666F\")\n")
cat("#let rule = rgb(\"#DCE1E5\")\n")
cat("#let accent = rgb(\"#C10016\")\n\n")

cat("#v(1.4cm)\n")
# The first line of the cover says that this is an example of the template,
# so that the framing is not left to the small print at the foot of the page.
cat("#text(size: 8pt, tracking: 1.6pt, fill: soft, ",
    ts(toupper("Company factsheet · Example")), ")\n", sep = "")
cat("#v(4pt)\n#line(length: 100%, stroke: 1.2pt + accent)\n#v(14pt)\n")
cat("#text(size: 25pt, weight: \"bold\", ", ts(display_name), ")\n", sep = "")
if (!is.na(subtitle_name)) {
  cat("#v(2pt)\n")
  cat("#text(size: 13pt, fill: soft, ", ts(subtitle_name), ")\n", sep = "")
}
cat("#v(3pt)\n")
cat("#text(size: 10.5pt, fill: soft, ",
    ts("Annual securities reports filed with the Financial Services Agency"),
    ")\n", sep = "")
cat("#v(26pt)\n")
cat("#grid(columns: (1fr, 1fr), column-gutter: 16pt,\n")
cat("  [#text(size: 8pt, weight: \"bold\", ", ts("The filer"),
    ")\n  #v(6pt)\n  ", typst_kv(identity_items), "],\n", sep = "")
cat("  [#text(size: 8pt, weight: \"bold\", ",
    ts(paste("Financial year", years[n_shown], "·", basis_label)),
    ")\n  #v(6pt)\n  ", typst_kv(summary_items), "]\n)\n", sep = "")
cat("#v(1fr)\n#line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.5pt + rule)\n#v(6pt)\n")
cat("#text(size: 7pt, fill: soft, ", ts(notice), ")\n", sep = "")
cat("#v(8pt)\n")
cat("#text(size: 7pt, fill: soft, ",
    ts(paste0("Compiled on ", format(Sys.Date(), "%d %B %Y"),
              ". Source: EDINET, Financial Services Agency of Japan.")),
    ")\n", sep = "")

# From here on every page carries the filer and the period in its head and
# its number in its foot.
cat("\n#set page(\n")
cat("  header: [#set text(size: 7pt, fill: soft)\n",
    "    #grid(columns: (1fr, auto), ",
    "[#text(weight: \"bold\", ", ts(display_name), ") #h(6pt) ",
    "#text(", ts(paste("Company factsheet ·", period_range)), ")], ",
    "[#text(", ts(paste("EDINET annual report data ·", basis_label)),
    ")])\n",
    "    #v(-4pt) #line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.5pt + rule)],\n", sep = "")
cat("  footer: [#set text(size: 7pt, fill: soft)\n",
    "    #line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.5pt + rule) #v(-2pt)\n",
    "    #grid(columns: (1fr, auto), ",
    "[#text(", ts("Source: annual securities reports, EDINET. Own calculations."),
    ")], [#context counter(page).display()])],\n", sep = "")
cat("  numbering: \"1\",\n)\n")
cat("```\n")
```

### How the figures are put together

```{r basis-note, results='asis'}
consolidation_sentence <- if (group_basis) {
  paste("**The consolidated accounts.** The filing states that it prepares",
        "consolidated financial statements, and every figure below is the",
        "group's unless it is marked ‡. A Japanese report states the",
        "parent company's own accounts beside the group's, under the",
        "dimension `NonConsolidatedMember`, and the two are far apart; the",
        "parent's series is in the same data and a factsheet of it is one",
        "setting away.")
} else if (has_group) {
  paste("**The parent company's own accounts.** The filing does state",
        "consolidated statements as well, and they have been set aside",
        "here because `consolidation` is set to \"nonconsolidated\".")
} else {
  paste("**The parent company's own accounts.** The filing states that it",
        "prepares no consolidated financial statements, so these are the",
        "only accounts there are. They carry the dimension",
        "`NonConsolidatedMember` in the conversion, which is where a reader",
        "of the tables will find them.")
}

basis_sentence <- if (basis == "as-reported") {
  paste("**As first reported.** Where the lake holds the annual report of a",
        "year, the figures of that year are the ones its own report states.",
        "A report also carries the year before it in its statements and four",
        "earlier years in its five-year summary; those are used only for a",
        "year whose own report is not in the lake, and every figure so taken",
        "is marked †.")
} else {
  paste("**As last reported.** The figures of a year are taken from the most",
        "recently filed annual report that states it, so a figure the filer",
        "restated is shown restated. Every figure that is not from the",
        "year's own report is marked †.")
}

two_axes <- paste(
  "**Two spans, and they are not the same.** The front matter of a Japanese",
  "annual securities report carries a five-year summary of the headline",
  "figures, 主要な経営指標等の推移, while its statements carry the year and",
  "its comparative. One report therefore affords five years of revenue, of",
  "the ordinary result, of total assets, of the three cash flows and of the",
  "employee count, and two years of everything that is a line of a",
  "statement. The tables of this factsheet follow that split instead of",
  "padding the short span out with dashes:",
  paste0("the summary covers ", period_range, " and the statements cover ",
         if (n_stmt > 1) paste0(stmt_years[1], " – ", stmt_years[n_stmt])
         else stmt_years[n_stmt], "."),
  "No figure of the summary is mixed into a statement table or the other way",
  "about.")

periods_note <- paste(
  "**The periods are resolved and not reported.** The agency's conversion",
  "carries no dates. It says which period a figure belongs to relative to",
  "the filing -- `CurrentYearDuration`, `Prior4YearDuration` -- and the",
  "module turns that into dates: for the current year and the comparative",
  "from the dates the filing states about itself, and for the earlier years",
  "by shifting whole years back from them. A filer whose years are not of",
  "equal length therefore has three of the five columns dated to the day by",
  "arithmetic rather than by its own statement. The column headings name the",
  "year the period ends in for that reason, and not a range of dates.")

marks_note <- paste(
  "**The marks.** † a figure the lake holds the year's own report for and",
  "which was nonetheless taken from a later one, which is a restatement.",
  "‡ a figure from the other consolidation basis, the chosen one stating",
  "none: the capital stock, the dividend per share and the payout ratio are",
  "properties of the company and not of the group, and a filer states them",
  "under the parent however it reports. § a figure from a concept the filer",
  "created for its own report rather than from the taxonomy, which is how an",
  "IFRS filer tags its operating profit. A mark belongs to a line read from",
  "a report; a line computed here from two others carries none, and the",
  "definitions say what each of those rests on. A change or a growth rate",
  "shown as · is one whose arithmetic would mislead, either end of it being",
  "negative: a smaller outflow and a fall are not the same thing and a",
  "column of percentages cannot tell them apart.")

# A year of the five-year summary whose own report is not in the lake is not
# a restatement and is not marked as one. It is worth saying how many of the
# columns stand on that footing, which is a property of the lake rather than
# of the filer.
held_years <- sum(as.character(shown$period_end) %in% names(own_filing))
coverage_note <- if (held_years >= n_shown) NULL else paste(
  "**The lake holds", nrow(annual), "annual",
  if (nrow(annual) == 1) "report" else "reports", "of this filer, covering",
  held_years, "of the", n_shown, "years shown.** The other",
  n_shown - held_years,
  if (n_shown - held_years == 1) "year is" else "years are",
  "the five-year summary of a later report, which is the only account of",
  "them there is here and is not a restatement of anything: no earlier",
  "report is in the lake to have said otherwise. Collecting the earlier",
  "reports is what would put each year's own statement of itself beside",
  "this one.")

for (sentence in c(consolidation_sentence, basis_sentence, two_axes,
                   coverage_note, periods_note, marks_note)) {
  cat(sentence, "\n\n")
}

if (!is.na(standards) && standards == "IFRS") {
  cat(paste("**An IFRS filer.** The filing reports under IFRS, and the",
            "elements of its consolidated statements and of its five-year",
            "summary are the ...IFRS spellings of the taxonomy. Its",
            "operating profit is a concept of the filer's own and is marked",
            "§ wherever it is shown. The ordinary result, 経常利益, does not",
            "exist under IFRS and is a dash for every year of the group;",
            "it is stated for the parent company, which reports under Japan",
            "GAAP, and the parent's series is one setting away.\n\n"))
}
if (nrow(stmt) == 1) {
  cat(paste("**One year of statements.** The lake holds a single annual",
            "report of this filer and that report states no comparative",
            "under a concept this factsheet reads, so the statement tables",
            "are one column wide and nothing is compared with anything.",
            "Collect the earlier reports to widen them.\n\n"))
}
```

## The filer

```{r profile, results='asis'}
# What the agency's list of filers says, which is not in the report: the
# industry, the address, whether the filer is listed and what day its year
# ends on. The list needs no API key and is a table of the Silver layer like
# the others.
profile_items <- list()
if (!is.null(filer_row)) {
  profile_items[["Name"]] <- coalesce(filer_row$name, filer_name_ja)
  profile_items[["Name in English"]] <- coalesce(filer_row$name_en,
                                                 filer_name_en, "–")
  profile_items[["Address"]] <- coalesce(filer_row$address, "–")
  profile_items[["Industry"]] <- coalesce(filer_row$industry, "–")
  profile_items[["Kind of filer"]] <- coalesce(filer_row$kind, "–")
  profile_items[["Listed"]] <- coalesce(filer_row$listed, "–")
  profile_items[["Stated capital"]] <- if (is.na(filer_row$capital)) {
    "–"
  } else {
    paste(fmt(as.numeric(filer_row$capital)), "JPY million")
  }
  profile_items[["Financial year ends"]] <- coalesce(filer_row$year_end, "–")
}

report_items <- list()
report_items[["Form"]] <- coalesce(dei_of("form"), "–")
report_items[["Cabinet Office ordinance"]] <- coalesce(dei_of("ordinance"), "–")
report_items[["Accounting standard"]] <- coalesce(standards, "–")
report_items[["Consolidated statements"]] <- if (is.na(consolidated_flag)) {
  "–"
} else if (consolidated_flag == "true") {
  "prepared"
} else {
  "none prepared"
}
report_items[["Period type"]] <- coalesce(dei_of("period_type"), "–")
report_items[["Correction"]] <- if (is.na(dei_of("amended"))) {
  "–"
} else if (dei_of("amended") == "true") {
  "yes"
} else {
  "no"
}
report_items[["Latest period"]] <-
  paste(format(tail(annual$period_start, 1), "%d %b %Y"), "–",
        format(tail(annual$period_end, 1), "%d %b %Y"))
report_items[["Document number"]] <- latest_filing

# Two tables rather than one: what the agency's list of filers says and what
# the report says about itself are different sources and are not mixed.
kv_rows <- function(items, heading) {
  out <- tibble(Field = names(items),
                Value = vapply(items, as.character, character(1)))
  print(knitr::kable(out, col.names = c(heading, ""), align = "ll"))
  cat("\n")
}

if (length(profile_items)) {
  kv_rows(profile_items, "As the agency lists the filer")
} else {
  cat("\n**As the agency lists the filer.** The table of filers is not in",
      "this Silver layer, so the industry, the address and the stated",
      "capital are not shown. A run of `update_bronze_edinet` collects the",
      "list, which needs no API key.\n\n")
}
kv_rows(report_items, "As the report describes itself")

# The agency's list and the filing can disagree about the one thing that
# decides which accounts these are, and for Kojima they do. It is worth
# saying so rather than quietly preferring one.
if (!is.null(filer_row) && !is.na(filer_row$consolidated) &&
    !is.na(consolidated_flag)) {
  listed_says <- filer_row$consolidated == "有"
  filing_says <- consolidated_flag == "true"
  if (listed_says != filing_says) {
    cat("\n**The two sources disagree.** The agency's list of filers says",
        "that this filer", if (listed_says) "has" else "has no",
        "consolidated accounts and its latest report says that it",
        if (filing_says) "prepared" else "prepared no",
        "consolidated financial statements. The report is what the figures",
        "are read from, and it decides the basis here.\n\n")
  }
}
```

```{r split-note, results='asis'}
# A jump in the issued share count is a split or a consolidation of the
# stock, and it matters here because a Japanese filer restates the per-share
# figures of its own five-year summary at its discretion and not always for
# every year of it. No factor is applied; the year is named instead.
moves <- shown %>%
  filter(!is.na(share_ratio),
         share_ratio > 1.5 | share_ratio < 1 / 1.5)
if (nrow(moves) > 0) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(moves))) {
    ratio <- moves$share_ratio[i]
    cat("\n", paste0("**The share count moved in ", moves$year[i],
                      "**, by a factor of ", fmt(ratio, 2)),
        if (ratio > 1) "— a split of the stock." else
          "— a consolidation of the stock.",
        "The per-share figures above are the ones the filer states, and a",
        "filer restates the earlier years of its own summary for a split at",
        "its discretion: Fujitsu's report restates four of its five years",
        "and leaves the fifth on the shares before the split. No factor has",
        "been applied here, because dividing a year the filer already",
        "restated would be wrong, so the per-share series above spans the",
        "move and the years either side of it do not rest on the same",
        "number of shares.\n\n")
  }
}
```

## Statement of operations

```{r income-note, results='asis'}
if (!is.na(standards) && standards == "IFRS") {
  cat(paste(
    "The statement below is the filer's consolidated income statement under",
    "IFRS, whose elements are those of the jpigp_cor taxonomy. The two lines",
    "a Japanese statement has and an IFRS one does not -- the ordinary",
    "result, 経常利益, and the extraordinary items, 特別損益 -- are a dash",
    "for every year, and the rows are left in rather than removed so that",
    "the shape of the statement this factsheet reads is the same whichever",
    "standard a filer reports under. The parent company of this group does",
    "report under Japan GAAP and does state an ordinary result; it is not",
    "shown here, because mixing it into a group statement would put a figure",
    "of a different company under a different standard into the same",
    "column.\n\n"))
  if (!all(is.na(shown_stmt$pretax_discontinued))) {
    cat(paste(
      "**The result before tax is of the continuing operations.** The",
      "element the taxonomy names for it carries the result of the",
      "operations the filer is continuing, and the result of those it",
      "discontinued is stated separately and is not added into it. The row",
      "beneath it carries that figure, and the checks at the end of this",
      "document show the difference rather than hiding it.\n\n"))
  }
} else {
  cat(paste(
    "A Japanese profit and loss account has two results where an IFRS or a",
    "US GAAP one has a single operating line. The operating result,",
    "営業利益, is the result of the business; the ordinary result, 経常利益,",
    "adds the recurring items outside it -- interest, dividends received,",
    "the share of the results of affiliates -- and is the figure a Japanese",
    "reader looks at first. Below it the extraordinary items, 特別損益,",
    "carry the gains and losses on disposals and the impairments, which an",
    "IFRS statement would show within the operating result.\n\n"))
}
```

```{r income-statement}

## The workforce

The ordinance asks a filer for the number of its employees, their average age,
their average length of service and their average annual pay. Neither the
ESEF nor the SEC regime requires anything of the kind, and these are stated
for the parent company whatever basis the rest of the report is on.

```{r workforce-table}
workforce <- pick(workforce_concepts, workforce_units)
workforce_latest <- workforce %>% arrange(key, desc(prd_end)) %>%
  group_by(key) %>% slice(1) %>% ungroup()

workforce_of <- function(key) {
  value <- workforce_latest$value[workforce_latest$key == key]
  if (length(value) == 0) NA_real_ else value
}

items <- tibble(
  item = c("Employees, at the year end",
           "Temporary workers, average over the year",
           "Average age, years",
           "Average length of service, years",
           "Average annual pay, JPY thousand"),
  value = c(fmt(tail(shown$employees, 1)),
            fmt(tail(shown$temporary_workers, 1)),
            fmt(workforce_of("average_age"), 1),
            fmt(workforce_of("average_service"), 1),
            fmt(workforce_of("average_salary") / 1e3))
)
knitr::kable(items, col.names = c(paste("The filer at", years[n_shown]), ""),
             align = "lr")
```

## The holders of the shares

```{r holders-table, results='asis'}
# The ten largest holders, which the ordinance asks for by name. The name and
# the holding are tagged against the same member -- No1MajorShareholdersMember
# and so on -- so the two are joined on it rather than on their order in the
# file.
holder_facts <- facts_all %>%
  filter(filing == latest_filing,
         grepl("^No[0-9]+MajorShareholdersMember$", dimensions))

rank_of <- function(dimension) {
  as.integer(sub("^No([0-9]+)MajorShareholdersMember$", "\\1", dimension))
}

names_held <- holder_facts %>%
  filter(local == "NameMajorShareholders", !is.na(text)) %>%
  transmute(rank = rank_of(dimensions), name = text)
shares_held <- holder_facts %>%
  filter(local == "NumberOfSharesHeld", !is.na(value)) %>%
  transmute(rank = rank_of(dimensions), shares = value)
share_of <- holder_facts %>%
  filter(local == "ShareholdingRatio", !is.na(value)) %>%
  transmute(rank = rank_of(dimensions), ratio = 100 * value)

holders <- names_held %>%
  full_join(shares_held, by = "rank") %>%
  full_join(share_of, by = "rank") %>%
  arrange(rank)

if (nrow(holders) > 0) {
  out <- tibble(
    `#` = as.character(holders$rank),
    Holder = coalesce(holders$name, "–"),
    `Shares, thousand` = fmt(holders$shares / 1e3),
    `Share, %` = fmt(holders$ratio, 2))
  print(knitr::kable(out, align = "clrr"))
  cat("\n")
  cat("The share is of the shares issued less the treasury shares, as the",
      "ordinance defines it, and it is the filer's own figure. The names are",
      "as the report writes them.\n\n")
} else {
  cat("The latest report states no table of major shareholders under the",
      "elements this factsheet reads. A filer other than a company -- a fund",
      "or a partnership -- has none to state.\n\n")
}
```

### The structure of the register

```{r holder-structure, results='asis'}
# The share of each class of investor, which the ordinance tags under an
# element of its own per class rather than against a dimension. The figures
# are fractions and are brought onto percentages here.
classes <- facts_all %>%
  filter(filing == latest_filing, local %in% holder_classes, !is.na(value)) %>%
  arrange(desc(prd_end)) %>%
  group_by(local) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()

structure_table <- tibble(class = names(holder_classes),
                          local = unname(holder_classes)) %>%
  left_join(classes %>% select("local", "value"), by = "local") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  mutate(share = 100 * value)

if (nrow(structure_table) > 0) {
  out <- tibble(Class = structure_table$class,
                `Share, %` = fmt(structure_table$share, 2))
  print(knitr::kable(out, align = "lr"))
  cat("\n")
}

register_items <- tibble(
  item = c("Shareholders on the register",
           "Shares constituting one unit",
           "Dividends declared for the year, JPY million"),
  value = c(fmt(count_of("shareholders_total")),
            fmt(count_of("unit_shares")),
            fmt(count_of("dividends_total") / scale)))
knitr::kable(register_items, col.names = c("The register", ""),
             align = "lr")
```

## Coverage of the tags

```{r coverage}
# What each concept list found and what it did not. The question a Japanese
# conversion raises is not whether a figure is in the data -- the whole
# report is, extensions included -- but whether the element this factsheet
# looked for is the element the filer used, which depends on the accounting
# standard and on the filer's own presentation.
coverage_of <- function(concepts, chosen, periods, what) {
  tibble(
    List = what,
    `Keys` = length(concepts),
    `Found` = length(unique(chosen$key[chosen$prd_end %in% periods])),
    `Years` = length(periods),
    `Figures` = sum(chosen$prd_end %in% periods))
}

coverage <- bind_rows(
  coverage_of(summary_concepts, summary_facts, shown$period_end,
              "Five-year summary"),
  coverage_of(statement_concepts, statement_facts, shown_stmt$period_end,
              "Statements"))
knitr::kable(coverage, align = "lrrrr")
```

```{r coverage-detail, results='asis'}
missing_of <- function(concepts, chosen, periods) {
  setdiff(names(concepts), unique(chosen$key[chosen$prd_end %in% periods]))
}

report_missing <- function(concepts, chosen, periods, what) {
  gone <- missing_of(concepts, chosen, periods)
  if (length(gone) == 0) {
    cat("\n**", what, ".** Every key of the list was found.\n\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  cat("\n**", what, ".** ", length(gone), " of ", length(concepts),
      " keys were not found on the ", tolower(basis_label),
      " basis. Each is shown as a dash wherever it appears.\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("| Key | Elements looked for |\n|:---|:---|\n")
  for (key in gone) {
    cat("| ", key, " | `", paste(concepts[[key]], collapse = "`, `"),
        "` |\n", sep = "")
  }
  cat("\n")
}

report_missing(summary_concepts, summary_facts, shown$period_end,
               "The five-year summary")
report_missing(statement_concepts, statement_facts, shown_stmt$period_end,
               "The statements")
```

### Figures refused for their unit

```{r refused, results='asis'}
# A fact whose unit is not of the class its key expects. This is where
# Fujitsu's equity ratio lands: the element is the one named for a ratio and
# the unit says it is an amount per share, so it is refused and the equity
# ratio is taken from the element that carries one.
if (nrow(refused) == 0) {
  cat("No fact was refused. Every figure taken carried the unit its line",
      "expects: an amount in yen, a count of shares, an amount per share or",
      "a pure number for a ratio.\n\n")
} else {
  out <- refused %>%
    distinct(key, concept, unit, class) %>%
    arrange(key) %>%
    transmute(Key = key, Element = paste0("`", concept, "`"),
              `Unit stated` = unit,
              `Unit expected` = vapply(class, function(cl)
                unit_classes[[cl]], character(1)))
  print(knitr::kable(out, align = "llll"))
  cat("\n")
  cat("A fact above was not used, its unit not being the one its line",
      "expects. This is a check on the elements and not on the filer: an",
      "element named for a ratio that carries an amount per share is a",
      "figure that would be printed as a percentage in the hundreds, and the",
      "line it belongs to is taken from an element whose unit fits.\n\n")
}
```

### Where each figure came from

```{r provenance-table}
# The three marks, counted. Under the "as-reported" basis with every report
# in the lake there is nothing in the first column by construction.
origin <- provenance %>%
  group_by(table) %>%
  summarise(
    Figures = n(),
    `Restated †` = sum(superseded),
    `No own report` = sum(!held),
    `Other basis ‡` = sum(source_basis == "other"),
    `Own concept §` = sum(extension),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(List = recode(table, summary = "Five-year summary",
                       statements = "Statements")) %>%
  select("List", everything(), -"table")
knitr::kable(origin, align = "lrrrrr")
```

```{r extensions, results='asis'}
ext <- provenance %>% filter(extension) %>% distinct(key, concept)
if (nrow(ext) > 0) {
  cat("\nThe figures taken from a concept the filer created for its own",
      "report, marked § in the tables:\n\n")
  cat("| Key | Element |\n|:---|:---|\n")
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(ext))) {
    cat("| ", ext$key[i], " | `", ext$concept[i], "` |\n", sep = "")
  }
  cat("\nAn element under a prefix built from the form and the filer's own",
      "EDINET code is one the filer created. The core taxonomy has no",
      "operating profit for an IFRS filer, so an IFRS filer that states one",
      "in its five-year summary states it under a concept of its own; the",
      "name is the taxonomy's all the same, which is why matching on the",
      "local name finds it.\n\n")
}
```

### Checks on the figures

```{r checks}
# Each check is a statement that must hold if the figures were read
# correctly, tested against the latest year of the table it belongs to.
# `left` is given as a list of the figures that make it up rather than as
# their sum, so that a check none of whose parts the filer states is reported
# as unstated instead of as a sum of zeros differing from a total. Treating
# an absent line as nothing is what made an IFRS filer fail the check on its
# ordinary result -- a line it does not have -- with 0 against 409,034.
check <- function(what, parts, right, tolerance = 0.01) {
  parts <- parts[lengths(parts) > 0]
  stated <- unlist(parts)
  if (length(stated) == 0 || all(is.na(stated)) ||
      length(right) == 0 || is.na(right)) {
    return(tibble(Check = what, Figure = "–", Against = "–",
                  Result = "not stated"))
  }
  left <- sum(vapply(stated, function(x) if (is.na(x)) 0 else x, numeric(1)))
  scale_of <- max(abs(c(left, right)), 1)
  tibble(Check = what,
         Figure = fmt(left / scale),
         Against = fmt(right / scale),
         Result = if (abs(left - right) / scale_of <= tolerance) "holds"
                  else "differs")
}

# A figure to be subtracted, which stays unstated when the filer states none.
# `-coalesce(x, 0)` would turn an absent line into a stated zero and make a
# check out of nothing: an IFRS filer has no extraordinary items, and the
# check on its ordinary result read 0 against 409,034 rather than saying that
# neither line is in the statement.
neg <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x)) NA_real_ else -x
}

# The pre-tax result of an IFRS statement is of the continuing operations
# and the result of the discontinued ones is stated beside it, so the two
# have to be added before the tax is taken off: Fujitsu's 409,034 and
# 146,904 less 100,737 of tax is 455,201 against a stated 454,636.
pretax_parts <- if (all(is.na(shown_stmt$pretax_discontinued))) {
  list(cur_stmt$pretax, neg(cur_stmt$income_taxes))
} else {
  list(cur_stmt$pretax, cur_stmt$pretax_discontinued,
       neg(cur_stmt$income_taxes))
}

checks <- bind_rows(
  check("Assets equal liabilities and net assets",
        list(cur_stmt$assets),
        coalesce(cur_stmt$liabilities_and_net_assets,
                 cur_stmt$liabilities + cur_stmt$net_assets)),
  check("Current and non-current assets sum to the total",
        list(cur_stmt$current_assets, cur_stmt$noncurrent_assets),
        cur_stmt$assets),
  check("Current and non-current liabilities sum to the total",
        list(cur_stmt$current_liabilities, cur_stmt$noncurrent_liabilities),
        cur_stmt$liabilities),
  check("Revenue less the cost of sales is the gross profit",
        list(cur_stmt$revenue, neg(cur_stmt$cost_of_sales_shown)),
        cur_stmt$gross_profit_shown),
  check("The gross profit less SG&A is the operating profit",
        list(cur_stmt$gross_profit_shown, neg(cur_stmt$sgna)),
        cur_stmt$operating_income),
  check("The operating profit and the non-operating items are the ordinary profit",
        list(cur_stmt$operating_income, cur_stmt$nonoperating_income,
             neg(cur_stmt$nonoperating_expenses)),
        cur_stmt$ordinary_income),
  check("The ordinary profit and the extraordinary items are the pre-tax profit",
        list(cur_stmt$ordinary_income, cur_stmt$extraordinary_income,
             neg(cur_stmt$extraordinary_loss)),
        cur_stmt$pretax),
  check("The pre-tax profit less tax is the profit",
        pretax_parts, cur_stmt$profit_group, tolerance = 0.02),
  check("The current and deferred tax sum to the tax charge",
        list(cur_stmt$income_taxes_current, cur_stmt$income_taxes_deferred),
        cur_stmt$income_taxes),
  check("The profit splits between the parent and the minorities",
        list(cur_stmt$profit, cur_stmt$profit_nci),
        cur_stmt$profit_group),
  check("The components of equity sum to the total",
        list(cur_stmt$equity_component_sum),
        cur_stmt$net_assets),
  # Across the two spans: the summary and the statements must agree about the
  # year they share, and this is the one check that tests the reading of both.
  check("The summary and the statements agree on revenue",
        list(shown$revenue[match(tail(shown_stmt$period_end, 1),
                                 shown$period_end)]),
        cur_stmt$revenue),
  check("The summary and the statements agree on total assets",
        list(shown$assets[match(tail(shown_stmt$period_end, 1),
                                shown$period_end)]),
        cur_stmt$assets),
  # Against the equity of the parent's own holders and not the total: a
  # filer computes its equity per share on what belongs to them, so a group
  # with a non-controlling interest would fail a comparison with the whole.
  # The remaining difference is the treasury, the per-share figure resting
  # on the shares outstanding and this one on the shares issued.
  check("The equity per share times the shares issued is the parent's equity",
        list(cur$equity_per_share * cur$shares_issued),
        coalesce(cur_stmt$equity_parent, cur$equity), tolerance = 0.05)
)
knitr::kable(checks,
             col.names = c(paste0("At ", tail(stmt_years, 1),
                                  ", JPY million"),
                           "Figure", "Against", ""),
             align = "lrrl")
```

```{r checks-note, results='asis'}
differ <- checks %>% filter(Result == "differs")
if (nrow(differ) > 0) {
  cat("\n", paste0(
    nrow(differ),
    if (nrow(differ) == 1) " of the checks above does not hold."
    else " of the checks above do not hold.", " ",
    paste("A check that differs is not by itself an error of the filing. The",
          "equity per share rests on the shares outstanding rather than on",
          "the shares issued, so a filer holding treasury shares misses that",
          "one by the treasury. A filer that presents an operating income or",
          "expense between its gross profit and its operating result leaves",
          "that check short by it. And a line this factsheet does not read",
          "leaves any sum it belongs to short of its total; the coverage page",
          "names every line it looked for and did not find. The figures",
          "either side of each check are printed so that the difference can",
          "be read rather than guessed at.")), "\n\n")
}
```

## The reports behind the figures

```{r filings-table}
reports <- annual_all %>%
  arrange(desc(submitted)) %>%
  transmute(
    Document = filing,
    Type = recode(doc_type, "120" = "Annual report",
                  "130" = "Correction", .default = doc_type),
    Period = ifelse(is.na(period_end), "–",
                    paste(format(period_start, "%d %b %Y"), "–",
                          format(period_end, "%d %b %Y"))),
    Filed = format(as.Date(submitted), "%d %b %Y"),
    `In this factsheet` = ifelse(filing %in% annual$filing, "yes", "no"),
    `English version` = ifelse(has_english == "1", "yes", "no"))
knitr::kable(reports, align = "lllllc")
```

```{r filings-note, results='asis'}
cat("A document number is the 書類管理番号, which is how the API addresses a",
    "filing and how the Bronze layer names the archive it holds. A report",
    "marked no above states a period another report in the lake states as",
    "well, and the basis decided which of them a figure came from.\n\n")

# The one deadline in this regime, and it is worth saying on the document
# rather than only in the module's documentation.
oldest <- min(as.Date(annual_all$submitted))
if (as.numeric(Sys.Date() - oldest) / 365.25 > 8) {
  cat("**The oldest report read here was filed", format(oldest, "%B %Y"),
      "**, which is within two years of the ten the agency keeps a filing",
      "retrievable for. What is older than ten years cannot be fetched",
      "again by any parameter of the API, so the Bronze layer of the lake",
      "is the only copy there will be.\n\n")
}
```

### What a figure rests on

```{r definitions, results='asis'}
definitions <- c(
  "Ordinary profit (経常利益)" = paste(
    "The result of the business and the recurring items outside it: interest",
    "paid and received, dividends received, the share of the results of",
    "equity-method affiliates, and the other non-operating income and",
    "expenses. It is the filer's own line and is not computed here. There is",
    "nothing to map it to under IFRS or US GAAP, and that is why the",
    "combined tables of this project do not carry it."),
  "Extraordinary items (特別損益)" = paste(
    "The gains and losses on disposals, the impairments and the other items",
    "the filer presents below the ordinary result. An IFRS statement shows",
    "the same events within the operating result, so the operating margins",
    "of a Japan GAAP filer and of an IFRS one are not the same measure."),
  "Equity ratio (自己資本比率)" = paste(
    "The filer's own, as stated in the five-year summary: the equity of the",
    "holders of the parent's shares over the total assets. The equity ratio",
    "of the balance sheet tables is computed here from the net assets less",
    "the non-controlling interests and the subscription rights, which is the",
    "same definition on the figures of the statement."),
  "Return on equity (自己資本利益率)" = paste(
    "The filer's own, as stated in the five-year summary. The return on",
    "assets beside it is computed here, on the average of the total assets",
    "at the start and the end of the year."),
  "Price-earnings ratio (株価収益率)" = paste(
    "The filer's own statement in its five-year summary, on the price at its",
    "own year end. It is the only price-based figure in this document and no",
    "price was fetched from anywhere."),
  "Total shareholder return (株主総利回り)" = paste(
    "The cumulative return on the shares over five years as a multiple of",
    "the value at the start, and beside it the return on the comparison",
    "index the filer names. Both are the filer's own statements, which the",
    "ordinance requires of a listed filer."),
  "Interest-bearing debt" = paste(
    "The sum of the short-term borrowings, the current portion of the",
    "long-term borrowings, the long-term borrowings, the bonds and the lease",
    "obligations, as the balance sheet states them. A Japanese balance sheet",
    "has no total for it and no filer tags one, so this is a sum of lines",
    "and a filer that presents a borrowing under a line this factsheet does",
    "not read is short of it by that line."),
  "EBITDA" = paste(
    "The operating profit and the depreciation and amortisation of the cash",
    "flow statement. It is computed here and is not a measure of the filer."),
  "Free cash flow" = paste(
    "The operating cash flow and the investing cash flow added together, the",
    "investing flow being negative where it is an outflow. It is computed",
    "here. The figure of the five-year summary table rests on the summary's",
    "own two flows and the one beside the statements on the statement's."),
  "Employees" = paste(
    "The count at the year end as the five-year summary states it, for the",
    "group where the figures are the group's and for the company otherwise.",
    "The average age, the length of service and the pay are of the parent",
    "company whatever the rest of the report is on, the ordinance asking",
    "for them of the filer itself."))

for (i in seq_along(definitions)) {
  cat("**", names(definitions)[i], ".** ", definitions[[i]], "\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

### Source and terms

```{r sources, results='asis'}
cat(paste(
  "**Source.** The annual securities reports of the filer, 有価証券報告書,",
  "as lodged with a Local Finance Bureau and published by the Financial",
  "Services Agency through EDINET. The figures are read from the agency's",
  "own conversion of the XBRL of each report to CSV, which the agency",
  "publishes beside the filing, and not from a third party's rendering of",
  "it. The list of filers is the agency's own Edinetcode list. Reuse of",
  "EDINET content is permitted under the terms the agency publishes on the",
  "disclosure site; this document reproduces figures of the reports and the",
  "names the reports state.\n\n"))

cat(paste(
  "**What is not here.** No price, no estimate, no forecast and no figure",
  "from any source but the reports themselves. The price-earnings ratio and",
  "the total shareholder return are the filer's own statements in its",
  "five-year summary, which is why they are in a document that fetches no",
  "market data. Nothing is adjusted for a share split; the note under the",
  "five-year summary says where one falls.\n\n"))

cat(paste(
  "**Produced by.** A template of fincommons, an open-source project for",
  "data lakes built from public financial data. The template is at",
  "`src/fincommons/financialreport/edinet/templates/` and reads the Silver",
  "layer of the edinet module; the figures of this document can be",
  "reproduced from the same lake by rendering it again.\n\n"))
```
